name: Workout Wednesday Run
description:
Join the Zwift Runners for a group run workout that will be of benefit to all distance runners.

The speeds for each group are based on a threshold speed of A group 15 kph, B 13 kph, C 11 kph, D 9 kph. We will start the intervals at that speed but increase the speed of the intervals we get into the workout. We encourage runners to choose the group closest to the effort level you want to run at and to keep to the nominal speed for that group to maintain the group dynamic. However if these speeds are significantly too low or high for you then you can choose to run in the group that is closest and then adjust the target speed up to 10% up or down in the game or via the Companion app.

If you have any questions about this event or want to find out more about Zwift Running in general then please visit the Zwift Runners Facebook group or zwift.com/run #gozwiftrun #wow

name: Power Loop
description:
Power Loop”, designed to enhance muscular endurance, cadence control, and
mental resilience. The session is FTP-based and includes motivational cues,
recovery phases, and a final push, making it ideal for riders looking to build
strength and rhythm indoors. 



A circuit of strength and control designed to push your limits and build resilience.




Perfect for developing muscular endurance, rhythm control, and mental toughness. Every loop prepares you for tougher challenges ahead—inside or on the road.



Interval Breakdown:



1. Warm-Up – 10 minutes



3 min in Z1 @ 90 RPM
3 min in Z2 @ 95 RPM
4 min in Z2 @ 100 RPM


2. Main Set – 4 Repeats of This Block (24 minutes total)



Each loop is a mix of tempo, threshold, and VO2 max work with controlled cadence variation:



2 min in Z3 @ 95 RPM — steady sub-threshold push
1 min in Z4 @ 85 RPM — near threshold, slower cadence
1 min in Z5 @ 75 RPM — VO2 max effort, low cadence strength
2 min in Z3 @ 90 RPM — flush with tempo effort
1 min in Z4 @ 100 RPM — FTP effort with fast legs
2 min in Z2 @ 85 RPM — recovery at sweet spot


3. Active Recovery – 5 minutes

5 min in Z1 @ 90 RPM


4. Final Push – 4 minutes

2 min in Z4 @ 90 RPM
2 min in Z5 @ 100 RPM


5. Cool Down – 5 minutes

5 min in Z1 @ 85 RPM

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

description:
Welcome to the Cycle Nation Warsaw Wake Up Call. Join us for a scientifically engineered PPP (Propel Progrssive Pace) session. We start with an easy warm-up pace and gradually increase power throughout the ride. In the last 10 minutes we activate three short intervals to really wake up your day! name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 1
description:
WTRL Team Time Trial #373

Our weekly WTRL Team Time Trial (TTT) allows teams of 3-8 Zwifters to race against the clock together throughout the day to achieve the fastest possible times. Teams are arranged into WTRL's unique Coffee Classes and feature both women's only Coffee Classes and mixed gender too.
  
 There are 30 racing events and teams can be registered up 30 minutes before each race event starts at www.wtrl.racing/ttt-home/ and you can pick your start time from the available slots. Each team is issued a unique RacePass that must be clicked by each team member to gain access to the event for sign-up. You'll also be able to check out the rules, course records and results which update live throughout the day.
  
 Teams & Riders must be registered with www.WTRL.racing and you'll need to be sharing data, via your Zwift Profile Connections with www.zwiftpower.com.
  
 If you are looking for a team, head to our dedicated WTRL TTT Facebook page where plenty of teams are always happy to welcome guest riders and new team mates (https://www.facebook.com/groups/WTRLTTT). Not on Facebook? Feel free to drop us an email with your preferred WTRL TTT Zone and current Zwift Category 
  
 #wtrl #wtrlttt

name: The XP Express with QueenBee Ladies
description:
All aboard The XP Express!

We're dishing out Double XP in this event so sign up, kit up and get ready to Level Up.

The XP Express is a turbocharged ride where every pedal stroke counts twice. Whether you're starting your Zwift journey or a seasoned pro, hop aboard to Level Up your ride.

How does it work?
The XP Express events will double your XP, helping you wrack up 40XP per kilometer or 64XP per mile! Leveling Up is the perfect way to unlock new swag, access to bikes and wheels, new routes and, of course, some bragging rights.

Use this event as an easy recovery ride, a quick warm up before your next race or push yourself to the limit to see how much XP you can earn.

name: Stage 2: Level Up Racing: BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits
description:
Level Up Racing is June’s ZRacing monthly series. Race across five stages from June 1 to July 5, with a new route each week and up to 250 XP waiting at every banner. Complete stages to build series progress, chase the GC leaderboard, and grab bonus XP as you race.

Stage 2

Dates: June 8–14
Route: BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits
Laps: 1
Distance: 22.1 km
Elevation: 243 m

Stage 2 brings BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits, a punchier test with more elevation and more chances to keep building XP. One lap, one effort, and another shot to add to your series total.

MONTHLY GC COMPETITION

Looking for extra motivation? The Monthly GC (General Classification) Competition lets you track your progress across all stages. Each race counts—your times add up throughout the series, shaping the overall standings. At the end of the month, the fastest total time takes the win!

VIEW RESULTS: http://zwift.com/racing/leagues/zracingjun2026
—------------------
Zwift Racing Score is aimed at pairing you with riders of similar racing abilities to keep racing fun, fair, and competitive. Read the FAQ here: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/racing-score-faq-BkG9_Rqrh


ADVANCED CATEGORY = 650+
CATEGORY RANGE 1 = 0-159 | 160-269 | 270-389 | 390-509 | 510-649
CATEGORY RANGE 2 = 0-209 | 210-329 | 330-449 | 450-569 | 570-724

For riders with a Racing Score of 650 or higher, the' Advanced' category will have separate events scheduled every other hour.

Please note that in order to enter the Advanced category, you will need the following:
Heart Rate Monitor
Zwift Racing Score of over 650
Smart Trainer/Bike or Power Meter


Hourly ZRacing will be split into five tighter categories for more exciting competition. Plus, with hourly alternating category ranges, you’ll have more options to find races that suit your level.

name: EVO CC Vortex Interval Ride [~3-3.8w/kg avg]
description:
Welcome to the Evolution Cycling Club [EVO] interval session. These rides are geared towards Zwifters that are looking for a varied content one hour session that can give them a full 5 zone workout. Draft in the group and stay zone 1-3, or move to the front and join the sprints for zones 4 and 5 for short bursts. Average for this ride will be mid to high Category B but it may vary based upon course/leader. There will be keepers at the back, and they will try hard to save dropped riders. The group is based upon high social interaction so bring your best banter. Use the mobile app or a keyboard to communicate in-ride.

#evo

name: EVO CC Flux Ride [1.8 - 2.0w/kg avg]
description:
This is a Evolution Cycling Club [EVO] Social Event and ride for all. Your co-operation and teamwork is essential to the success of the ride and we ask that all riders respect the pace set by the leader (Yellow Beacon). We may include intervals over and below the ride average advertised power range, but we will allow enough recovery and time to regroup after every effort. This is not a race, so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong we would welcome any help offered by stronger riders to bring any dropped riders back to the yellow beacon. We welcome good chat and a social atmosphere for new and experienced Zwifters alike, everyone is welcome.

#evo

name: INC Relentless Intervals
description:
Suitable for A riders as a base session, or B & C riders wanting to push themselves.

Examples of the drills are – Z2 with 15sec Z5/6 bursts every 6minutes, alternating Z2/Z3 in various durations, Z2 - Z4 ramps of decreasing duration and many other sessions.

All sessions will be around 60-90mins and will include a warm up so just grab your bottles and head straight to the pen.

This is an Innovation Cycling Training Ride Event – all riders are welcome. These events are put together to push you further than before, if you are feeling fresh hop on the front, if you need rest surf the draft. This training ride is part of the INC RELENTLESS training rides that happen daily with each day focusing on a different area of improvement.

Tips: Use the draft to rest and ensure you do not lose the draft.

name: SZR Early Birdies
description:
Welcome to SZR Early Birdies

This is a group ride with the focus on remaining together. The average pace PRIOR to any race finish will be 2.2 wkg. Sprints and intervals will be added at the discretion of the leader and we will at time ride above and below the advertised pace!

Please regroup quickly after sprints, intervals or hills and sit between the yellow and red beacons.
This ride will particularly benefit D and lower C riders looking to get stronger.

name: 3R VOLT Interval Ride [~2.6-3.2 w/kg avg]
description:
This is a 3R Group Ride so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong, please help the keeper beacon (Red) to assist other riders back to the pack. 3R VOLT runs five days a week and is designed to provide a solid and fun training platform for riders.

Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.8-3.2 w/kg.

The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides and training needs, the following is a typical week:
Monday – After what has hopefully been a fun backed weekend on the bike, this our recovery session
Tuesday – Tends to be more of a classic interval session, riders usually finish with an average of around 3.0w/kg
Wednesday – We take to the hills and one of our tougher sessions with riders averaging around 3.2w/kg
Thursday – is our no red beacon ride and again tough interval sets and riders finishing around 3.2w/kg
Friday - is a little different, we don't take ourselves too seriously and often play a variety of games and quizzes along side the intervals and riders end up with around 2.8-3.0w/kg

The rides are typically around an hour long, but some may take up to 75mins with the majority finishing with either a ramp or a mini race.

The group welcomes rider interaction through messaging and the VOLT discord server and features a friendly bunch of regulars to which newcomers, and riders stepping up from lower intensity rides, are always welcome. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/

This group ride is not a race so. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #Ride3R #RideRaceRaise.

name: 3R SPARK Interval Ride [~2.2-2.5 w/kg avg]
description: This is a 3R Group Ride Event (not a race). 3R Spark runs five days a week and is designed to be an accessible and sociable training session, aimed primarily at riders is Cat-D. Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.0-2.5 W/kg. The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides. Mondays and Tuesdays are our entry-level steady-state rides, where we aim to hold a steady 2.0-2.2 throughout. Wednesdays are a steady recovery ride, where we split into two different ability groups. Thursdays and Fridays are our interval sessions, designed to help Cat D riders push themselves a little further. For interval sessions we aim to average between 2.2-2.5 for the session, but there will be times above and below. Thursday and Friday sessions often include an optional mini-race at the end. Rides are typically around an hour long. Spark is a great introduction to group rides on Zwift, we are a friendly and supportive group who love to see one another succeed. We always have a sweeper (red beacon) whose wheel you can grab if you get dropped. There’s always plenty of good chat, via in-ride messages or on Discord. Come and join us! Join the 3R Facebook group for more info: https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #3R #RideRaceRaise

name: Endure IQ Training Squad Session
description:
SESSION FOCUS:
The focus of this session is on building your tolerance to intensities similar
to those during a 70.3 triathlon. You will be working in the L3b training
zone. You should hope to see reduced HR drift within this zone as you complete
more of these sessions. From a physiological perspective, these sessions help
promote fat oxidation, and structural changes at a muscular level, such as
increased mitochondrial content and capillarization.

WARM-UP:
20 min
PREP:
5 x 30'' L4 /30' L1
2 min recovery
MAIN SET:
20 min working around 70.3 pace (5 min up and 5 min under)
5' between sets
COOLDOWN:
10 min

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

name: MAAP In The Field: UK Group Ride
description:
MAAP In The Field: UK Group Ride

Join the MAAP crew each week, we’ll roll as a group at a moderate 2-2.5 w/kg pace. The course varies each week, with a range of undulating routes. Join our global community for a social ride and unlock the exclusive MAAP kit. Jump on the chat, ask us any questions you might have and remember that this isn’t a race, save that for Wednesdays!


How do I unlock the Off The MAAP Kit?


Not only will you be repping the kit in-event, but finish any of our weekly rides to unlock the Off The MAAP Kit in your garage, so you can proudly wear the M-Flag design on any ride.

About MAAP:

MAAP exists for the progression of cycling. An independent brand, we’re committed to bringing a new perspective on performance cycling apparel. Every piece that we design evokes our obsession with quality, function, and precision. Fabrics are hand-selected from premier Swiss and Italian mills and are constructed at the most respected factories across Europe. Using the feedback and support from racing teams and cyclists around the globe, our industry-leading product developers are relentlessly refining and evolving every product, season after season. Visit: maap.cc

Stay up to date with the latest MAAP In The Field rides, product launches, cycling events and see who’s topping the leaderboards each week. Connect with the global MAAP community by joining our MAAP Strava Club: https://www.strava.com/clubs/293623 for a global epic from our In the Field series, stay posted on our Facebook page: http://facebook.com/maap.cc or fill your feed via: https://www.instagram.com/maap.cc/.

name: The XP Express - Run
description: All aboard The XP Express! We're dishing out Double XP in this event so sign up, lace up your shoes and get ready to Level Up. The XP Express is the "super shoe" of Zwift running, where every stride counts twice. Whether you're starting your Zwift journey or a seasoned pro, hop aboard to Level Up your run. How does it work? The XP Express events will double your XP, helping you wrack up 80XP per kilometer or 120XP per mile! Leveling Up is the perfect way to unlock new swag, and of course some bragging rights. Use this event as an easy recovery run, a quick warm up before your next race or push yourself to the limit to see how much XP you can earn.

name: SZR Sunrise Ride
description:
Welcome to SZR Sunrise

C and D  Ride
Tempo ride with optional sprint sections. Non sprinters will work as a group to create as much draft as we can for the sprinters.
Sprints will be added at the discretion of the leader.
We will at times ride above and below the advertised pace, please don’t feel the need to tell the leader they will be aware but the ride average will be as advertised.
This is NOT a recovery ride, we work hard and work as a team.

E Ride
The focus is on the Group and keeping together while having fun to make the time fly fast!
The ride tempo is shown next to the ride category, this is rider weight / gender dependant.
Note that the average is for the ride prior to any optional faster finish (with a beacon).
The ride leader will aim (prior to any faster finish) to ride mid parameters after a short warmup period.
There might be slight variations above or below the average during the ride.


NB:
Please always respect the ride leader and follow his / her instructions.
The ride tempo is shown next to the ride category, this is rider weight / gender dependant.

name: Pride On with LGBTQ Zwifters
description:
LGBTQ Zwifters invite you to ride or race with us during Pride month in support of the LGBTQIA+ community.

Let’s clip in, turn up the colours, and roll out together! This Pride On social ride is all about togetherness - one big, joyful bunch cruising the roads where everyone belongs. No surges, no stress, no getting left behind. You can expect steady spins, good vibes, and plenty of chat as rainbow jerseys fill the screen. Whether you’re here to celebrate, support, or simply enjoy a relaxed ride with an amazing community, this is your space. Ride proud, ride together, and let’s make the miles brighter.


All Pride month events

Group rides:
Most rides will be community-led and rubberbanded (E cat) unless specified by the event pace category.

Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday.
01 - 7 June - Island Hopper
08 - 14 June - Hot Laps
15 - 21 June - Croissant
22 - 28 June - London Flat
29 & 30 June - Beach Island Loop

Sunday.
LGBTQz Ride with Pride club social ride. 

Races: 
Each Wednesday in June - Race with Pride in our fun and friendly crit format.
Each Saturday in June - Join us to Chase the Rainbows. Can you work together with others in your pace category to chase the rainbows in front, or keep the chasing rainbows at bay?

Pick up some exclusive rainbow swag with our different unlocks, including the chance to unlock vintage Pride On kits and socks on Throwback Thursdays!

Find out more about LGBTQ Zwifters at https://lgbtq-zwifters.com/

name: Kiwi Crew Ride
description:
Established in 2018 by former NZ Tour Pro Greg Henderson this Kiwi group ride is now a classic! Our community continues to grow with some of NZ's best E-Sports racers taking to the line each week.

The ride starts off at a moderate 2.5 w/kg average where there’s time for a bit of banter or to spin a good yarn so stay close as you don't want to miss out on the fun! But rachet up the shoes because at the 30 minute mark things get spicy with the Riot After Party! Race to the finish and see how long you can hang on or if you can take on some of the best!

Will you be this weeks Riot winner?

Please respect the ride and stay with the ride leader (yellow beacon) until the Riot hits with around 15 mins remaining, at that point you can race the riot to the finish, or cruise to the finish. Everyone is welcome to join.

* Everyone with a Power Meter and / or Smart Trainer is welcome to join.
* Use of the Coffee Stop during the Riot will incur a 1 min time penalty.
* New cadence rules in play.
* Winners subject to verification requests.

#kiwicrew

description:
Se cerchi la giusta compagnia per prepararti al fine settimana sei nel posto giusto.
Lo scopo della SPICY COFFEE ITALIAN RIDE è quello di stare tutti insieme, sfruttare la scia del gruppo e fare due chiacchiere ad un ritmo medio fra i 2.0 e i 2.5 w/kg per 90 minuti, il late join è attivo per 30 minuti.
Questa NON è una gara.
Segui le istruzioni dei leader(giallo) per un gruppo compatto.
Ricordati di non superare la fence (barra rossa) altrimenti verrai eliminato.
Partecipa a questa ride per sbloccare la divisa del team italy.
BUONA PEDALATA A TUTTI
TEAM ITALY organizza una vasta gamma di eventi, tutti con le seguenti regole:
-in una pedalata di categoria D, alcuni ciclisti sono principianti, segui le istruzioni del
leader (logo giallo) che appaiono come testo al centro e tieni presente che il ritmo sarà fra i 2.0 e i 2.5 w/kg

capacità di utilizzare la scia e l'equipaggiamento della vostra bici in gioco
-abilitare i messaggi nelle opzioni zwift, fondamentali per una buona esperienza

corse C, facili per un A, 4w/kg ftp, impegnative per B 3.2 w/kg ftp, ed estreme per C con 2.5
w/kg ftp.

This is NOT A RACE.

Remember the Fence is KILLER, 60 seconds over and you'll be out of the event.
Join this ride to unlock the Team Italy Jersey.

beacon) that appear as text in the middle and keep in mind that the pace will be between 2.0 and 2.5 w/kg

capacity to use the draft and your in-game bike equipment
- enable the messages in Zwift options, fundamental for a great experience

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

The 4STAR Gravel Grind is here — a six-week racing block designed to push your limits across Zwift’s toughest mixed-terrain routes.

* 🇳🇿 9:30pm NZ / 7:30pm AUS

* Fun. Fitness. Friendships.

* Competitive, but always respectful — no egos, just effort

⸻

⚡ Why You’ll Love It

Clip in. Show up. Throw down.

name: 6Points Challenges Group Thursday Training Ride
description:
This is a TRAINING event, category D, with a yellow beacon leader. The beacon leader will ride up to a 2.5w/kg pace average wherever possible. The beacon may employ the fence at times.

Please look out for this training ride on Thursdays, every week, at 9.55am UTC in the UK, 4.55am EDT in the US, and at 10.55 CET in Europe. Use #6Points to search for our rides on the Zwift website.

This weekly 6Points Mallorca Thursday training ride is intended to provide a challenge for riders, and is open to all timezones. You should ride as a group, following the instructions of the beacon ride leader(s) for any sprints, intervals and spicy segments, regrouping after each when requested. All our group rides also have a closing minirace, to start from behind the beacon. The fence may be used to control starts for these spicy sections.
About the in-real-life Reverence 6Points Mallorca
The ultra-distance Reverence 6Points Mallorca real life cycling event, with Title sponsor Reverence Hotels, is ridden around Mallorca and raises money for charity, currently supporting Asdica, who work on behalf of disabled children, and Save-the-Med. Now in its third edition, it has already earned a reputation as a fun but tough event that epitomises cycling at its best. 6Points has raised over €100,000 for charities in this way over three years.

6Points Mallorca is a ride around the whole of the beautiful island of Mallorca, covering well over 420 kms, climbing 7500 metres and touching the four compass extremities, as well as the highest and lowest points of Mallorca, over 3 days. See https://6pointschallenges.com/ for more about our in-real-life events. We also run these events in Ibiza / Formentera and Menorca.

Like our Zwift group ride, 6Points Mallorca is NOT a race. It is an opportunity to participate in a challenging ride, with like-minded cyclists, to enjoy Mallorca’s diverse beauty and the friendship and camaraderie of fellow riders. 6Points supports sustainable cycling, whose riders care for the environment and practise courtesy to fellow road users.

We have organized our 6Points Zwift training ride series to suit what we believe is relevant to bike riders’ interests in performance and improvement, bearing in mind the in-real-life 6Points Mallorca challenge which is also ridden in groups with controlled pace.
The 6Points Zwift group ride
As we expect our riders to be able to ride up to 100 miles at or around a 15mph average on our irl (in-real-life) rides, such steady riding members should be comfortable with Zwift Category D. Beacon leaders communicate via Zwift message (always) and/or Discord (sometimes) to vary the pace to allow for sprints, intervals and optionally a mini-race towards the end of the rides, with regrouping after each sprint. Make as much use of drafting as you can, for more effective sprinting and rest intervals.

During the ride, the beacon will announce any sprints, and the ride will finish with a minirace to the end of the ride of between 3kms and 8kms depending on the course. The Beacon will announce this too.

Results (the finishing order, relevant to the minirace which we will all start together) can be seen at the end of the ride on screen, and we will, in common with many other ride series, publish your results on zwiftpower.com too, based on the ride category D.

All bikes and Power-Ups (PU) are allowed, but it is better not to use TT bikes to ensure drafting. Please add 6Points (X) to your Zwift name to allow your ride presence to be recognized, where X is your own ride category. Categories in Zwift are related to your Functional Threshold Power (FTP); use your FTP and then divide by your weight in kg to get the W/kg that applies to you.

On this ride series, all riders and categories are welcome, but bear in mind that rides are designed for:

Category D: 2 W/kg to 2.5 W/kg FTP. The beacon leader will ride to 2.5w/kg pace average or below.

PLEASE NOTE: Strava data for our rides must be open (not private or hidden). Please use a heart rate monitor so that we can monitor correlated power and heart rate to help assure fair riding.

You can use our Discord channel to talk to each other at https://discord.gg/bPsQCNh

Please see the 6Points Zwift page link at https://6pointschallenges.com for more, including how we support our chosen charities.

https://6pointschallenges.com/

#6points

name: DIRT 505 Thursday Endurance Ride
description:
Welcome to the DIRT 505 Thursday Endurance Ride!

Please join us weekly on Thursdays at a pace of 2.6-2.8w/kg for 90 minutes.

The 505 rides take place Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for 90 minutes at the same time and same consistent pace. Saturday's we ride for 120 minutes.

We kick off our rides with a 5 minute pace at 2.2w/kg to get us warmed up and together as a team. The fence is used throughout the ride to keep everyone together. The fence will not kick you off the ride but we do encourage all our riders to stay together as close to the beacon as possible. Our rides offer a 30 minute late join option.
The ride leader will stay as close to ride pace as possible. We try to change up the routes each week and some of the routes may include some small to moderate climbs.

Our group exists to encourage and build up cyclists around the world no matter your time zone, fitness level, pro or amateur. We exist to encourage and build up a team culture of unity in the cycling community.

name: The Chop by AHDR
description:
AHDR THE CHOP

Being "in the chop" is an Aussie expression that you won't read about in the UCI rulebook. It's one of the many nuances of bike racing that only comes with experience.

Sometimes when you're in a race and find yourself in the final break-away bunch you might get asked "are we in the chop?" or "are we chopping it?". This is referring to collusion between the lead riders to work together until the finish. Many times a break-away will be doomed in the final kilometres because everyone starts playing cat and mouse, attacking, sitting up, etc.

But all that goes out the window in the last lap. This is generally where the group comes together and the final push begins. Working together goes out the window and is every man or woman for themselves for the final sprint to the line.

AHDR The Chop is a flat fast time-based handicap race. Do you always get blown out the back on the start of a multi grade race trying to hang onto the guy going with A grade pushing 5w/kg. Well not on The Chop. Released in Grades there are time splits from D to A with the intention of all coming together at the end for the big finish. Each Grade wears a different AHDR/Zwift kit making each grade easily identifiable on who's wheel you want to catch if they go past.

Races happen on Thursday evenings. We plan to add further races in the future. No single race has been the same. Many variables are at play on The Chop including course (which is generally a flat course), race numbers, and the inevitable sandbaggers. It has been called a team time trail and cat and mouse but the real racers know it only as "THE CHOP". Do you have what it takes to take the glory?

A Grade – AHDR GIANT Kit
B Grade – HDR Kit
C Grade – Fluoro Pink
D Grade – Fluoro Camo

#ahdr #cyclingaustralia

name: QT2 Systems Group Workout
description:
Join QT2 Systems for a challenging hour-long session, each Thursday morning at 5:15 AM EST, around some of the best routes on Zwift. Each 60-minute ride includes a quick warm-up and cool down. These workouts are designed to challenge and make you stronger along the way. One of our coaches is present, each week, to answer questions, motivate, and encourage riders throughout the entire workout.

With ZWIFT’s ride banding, these workouts are suitable for athletes of all levels, regardless of fitness level. That’s right, we are all “rubber-banded” together, relative to percentage of rider FTP.

QT2 Systems is one of the world’s premier triathlon coaching brands, and parent company to OutRival Racing, The Cycling Formula, The Core Diet, The Run Formula, and Cycle Life Studios.

name: 5K Down Under
description:
Join us for a 5k group run led by Australian age-group triathlete Ben Shepherd. Ben is an avid triathlete and Zwifter who - like many of us - balances his training with work and family. He's a thirty-something father of a young daughter and credits triathlon with helping him lose over 50lb (25kg). He's a Ironman World Championships finisher (2016) and has qualified to represent his native Australia at the ITU Age-Group World Championships in September of this year.

After suffering a tendon injury to his patella (kneecap), he's working back to fitness with 100% treadmill running and is happy to have some company! Join him for a relaxed pace 5K. Come just to run or to chat about triathlon, Zwift, or where to get the best flat whites. Ben will be leading at 5:30/km (8:50/mi) pace, but feel free to join in at your own pace. This is a social run, not a race, so leave the racing flats at home for now.

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

name: GRIT Tempo-ish Thursday
description:
This is a group ride that has competitive sprint segments. Although not mandatory, riders are encouraged to participate in sprints. After each sprint we quickly regroup and continue the tempo paced lap. The motto of the ride has always been "Faster and farther together". Come have fun with us as we train to improve sprinting capability.

We ride a course that is approx. 5 km (3 miles) and we continue laps for 60 minutes. Each lap has a timed sprint zone and we sprint at this area on each lap for about 7 sprints in the 60 minute ride.

The tempo pace is around 3.0 w/kg and we normally have a large peloton of 30+ riders moving at this pace.

Sprints are short duration (10 - 30 seconds) and will be competitive as riders use maximum power to compete for the fastest sprint time.

description:
Please join us on Phoenix Rising As One and, at least for a little while, overcome some of those annoying real life stresses. Phoenix Rising As One is a joyful social group ride. We welcome riders of all types and strengths to join us for an hour of fun and camaraderie. 

The yellow beacon will attempt to ride at a pace of between 1.5 and 1.8 w/kg.  There will be no fence and we welcome riders to ride at whatever pace they want – the objective of the ride is to be together which we are via text and discord.  And we will have a fab group of sweepers to accompany and inspire riders who wish to ride at a gentler pace.  We intend that no one ride alone unless they want to.

We will ride a variety of routes, attempting to cover some of the less traveled routes in Zwift and earning the occasional badge.  We will ride flattish routes although some nasty shorter climbs or non paved surfaces will inevitably be included. 

So wherever you are located, please join us for a rollicking fun hour of cycling.

name: CRYO-GEN: The Tempo Split
description:
Push your limits, find your rhythm.
Welcome to The Tempo Split, a dynamic tempo session designed to help you build aerobic power and endurance. This isn’t just a group ride; it’s a choose-your-own-adventure workout where you decide how deep to dig.

How it Works
We all start together in a single pen for a 10-20 minute progressive warm-up at a controlled, social pace. Once the warm-up is complete, the “Split” begins.
The Yellow Beacon (Lead): Will begin intervals at a high-tempo pace of 3.2 – 3.5 w/kg. This is for those looking to challenge their sustained power.
The Red Beacon (Sweep): Will begin intervals at a steady tempo pace of 2.7 – 3.0 w/kg. This is the safety net for those who want a solid workout without going “into the red.”

The Challenge
Start with the Yellow Beacon. Your goal is to hold that higher intensity for as long as possible. If the effort becomes unsustainable or your heart rate climbs too high, don’t worry—simply ease back to the Red Beacon following behind and finish the interval with that group.

Course & Intensity Notes
Please note that this is a flexible training session:
Terrain Impact: The ride format and group cohesion may change based on the route’s profile. Expect paces to shift slightly on climbs or descents.
Variable Intervals: Interval intensity and duration are subject to change week-to-week based on the specific goals of the session and the total distance of the chosen course.

Pro Tip: Use the draft! Whether you’re with the Yellow or Red group, staying tucked in a pack will help you maintain these tempo zones more efficiently.
Pro Tip: Keep an eye on the on-screen chat. The Beacons will announce interval starts, finishes, and any adjustments to the target w/kg based on the terrain.

Ride Rules
Be Kind: This is a supportive training environment.
Listen to your body: There is no shame in dropping back to the Red Beacon; that’s exactly why it’s there!
Stay Predictable: Avoid sudden surges so the groups can stay formed.

name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 10
description:

Our weekly WTRL Team Time Trial (TTT) allows teams of 3-8 Zwifters to race against the clock together throughout the day to achieve the fastest possible times. Teams are arranged into WTRL's unique Coffee Classes and feature both women's only Coffee Classes and mixed gender too.

Each team is issued a unique RacePass that must be clicked by each team member to gain access to the event for sign-up. You'll also be able to check out the rules, course records and results which update live throughout the day.

name: Know No Bounds Ride
description:
Welcome to the #KnowNoBounds Ride! A ride where we explore the boundaries (or lack thereof) on Zwift.
The ride will begin with 30 minutes at 3 w/kg, utilizing the fence to keep riders together. At the end of the 30 minutes, riders are free to do as they please:
they can stay together and explore the chosen course for the day, or they can head off to the nearest mountain with friends and race it!

When the 30 minute "fenced" portion of the ride is over, we will #KnowNoBounds. Have bike, will travel.
If needed, you will be able to turn to ride in opposite direction on the circuit to reconnect with the group quicker (if you need restroom or are dropped),
and most importantly, the group is not limited to the in-game courses. We can choose to go up a mountain, along a riverside, or any road we want to!

We’re on a mission: to set everyday cyclists free to explore without limits. And we’re going by bike.

Community and camaraderie in cycling is everything: group chat on this ride is highly encouraged!

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

description:

What is Racing Score?

Racing Score is an intuitive system that replaces the traditional categories (A - D) with a 0-1000 scale to reflect your current level, considering various metrics like race performances and power. This score helps Zwift recommend the most competitive band to race in, ensuring a fun, rewarding, and exciting experience as you track your progression throughout your Zwift racing adventures.

WHAT IS ZWIFT POWER? For further information on connecting to Zwift Power check out this support page: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/connecting-to-zwiftpower-SyldRc_4H

Please note; for your results to show up in Zwift Power you must be using a Heart Rate Monitor (HRM) and be riding on a smart trainer, smart bike, or using a power meter.

description:
Whether you’re a Tour de France hopeful, a procrastinating amateur, or the person whose front tire spends a suspicious amount of time in someone else’s rear derailleur...we honestly don't care!

There are no "real" awards for winning a climb or clinching a sprint. If you’re looking for a trophy, try a middle school soccer tournament.

The goal is to maintain a steady engine...smooth rotations and clean pulls. Even when the profile gets punchy or the wind shifts, we're staying "dialed in" on 18–20 mph (30–32 kph).

Feeling a little gapped? Don't sweat it. We strive to have a dedicated sweeper on every ride to help pull you back into the fold.

The "Gene Autry" Philosophy: We believe in freedom! As the legend himself said, we won’t fence you in.

At the end of the day, you’re the captain of your own bike. Whether you’re pushing the pace or soaking in the scenery: ride your ride!

So come out, enjoy the virtual fresh air, and keep the faith!

We don’t care if you’re a contender, pretender, or rear-ender!  We just enjoy riding with others in a fun, social group. 

There are no “real” awards for being first on a climb or on a sprint during our rides, only the satisfaction of being able to ride a bike for just one more day!

Also, we will be applying the Gene Autry philosophy…we won’t fence you in!

Remember, the choice is yours…ride your ride!

So, enjoy your ride, keep the faith, and become that someone!

name: BMTR Chase Adventure
description:
Why is this event called a “Chase Adventure?” Because it allows each participant to explore the upper reaches of their personal power map (zones) — primarily Zones 3 and 4 — while collaborating with other like-minded explorers on a similar journey, all sharing the same goal: to get stronger, fitter, and faster. This “adventure” gives each participant an opportunity to expand their personal “power map” and reach new heights of achievement. 

As BMTR is known for having the “highest chat per kilogram” on Zwift 😀, participants will also enjoy fun, friendly banter and benefit from the support and camaraderie of their teammates and ride leader as they navigate this “adventure” together!

Ride Leaders will coordinate the B, C, and D Category teams to keep their effort levels within the advertised average w/kg range. The A Category team will self-organize their effort level.


**HOW THE "CHASE" IS SET UP**
Four teams will start at different intervals: Team D goes first, followed by Teams C,  B, and finally A. The goal is for Teams A, B, and C to catch up with Team D near the finish line by working as a Team at their designated w/kg paces

When faster teams catch up to slower ones, riders can join them to increase their effort. Faster team members can also drop back to recover. If a rider can't keep up, they can return to their original group and try again the following week! 


**SWITCHING TEAMS AND SWEEPING DURING THE LATE JOIN PERIOD**
You have a 30-minute Late Join period to switch teams if your current team isn't at your desired pace. During this time, we won't conduct any sweeps, so please use the Late Join feature to rejoin your category group if you fall behind. To rejoin or switch teams, do not “quit” the event; instead, simply “exit/end,” save your ride, then rejoin your original team category or select a different one.


**AVERAGE W/KG RANGE CATEGORY CALCULATIONS**
The specified average watts per kilogram (w/kg) pace ranges for each Team represent the overall average for the entire event. During the event, teams may, at times, exceed or fall below this range. The respective category event averages are calculated to keep most riders within Zone 3 and 4 effort levels. This assumes that each rider selects a category that accurately reflects both their Functional Threshold Power (FTP) and their Zwift-assigned category.

We look forward to having you join us!

Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! name: Thursday Pizza Burner  🍕🔥
description:

Each week we spin through 100km of pristine Zwift roads, rotating between flattish routes to keep the endurance training fast and fun. Burn those pizza slices, chat about all things Zwift/cycling, and build your base with ride leader Eric Schlange, creator of Zwift Insider!

Get ready to build next-level fitness with our 9-week OutSeason cycling series! Join us every Tuesday and Thursday for a focused, one-hour session designed to boost your strength, endurance, and power. With just two workouts per week, you’ll start building winter strength that will prepare you to reach your goals next season. This program is tried-and-true, with over 10,000 athletes using it to succeed in cycling and triathlon for over 16 years.

Why settle for base miles alone when you can add targeted intensity this winter? Join Endurance Nation and see what a season of smart training can do. Discover more about the OutSeason at www.endurancenation.us/zwift.

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides on Saturdays, Sundays and Mondays each week — they are great alternates to these scheduled workouts!

Level Up Racing is June’s ZRacing monthly series. Race across five stages from June 1 to July 5, with a new route each week and up to 250 XP waiting at every banner. Complete stages to build series progress, chase the GC leaderboard, and grab bonus XP as you race.

Stage 2

name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 12
description:

name: Pride On with LGBTQ Zwifters
description:
LGBTQ Zwifters invite you to ride or race with us during Pride month in support of the LGBTQIA+ community.

Let’s clip in, turn up the colours, and roll out together! This Pride On social ride is all about togetherness - one big, joyful bunch cruising the roads where everyone belongs. No surges, no stress, no getting left behind. You can expect steady spins, good vibes, and plenty of chat as rainbow jerseys fill the screen. Whether you’re here to celebrate, support, or simply enjoy a relaxed ride with an amazing community, this is your space. Ride proud, ride together, and let’s make the miles brighter.


All Pride month events

Group rides:
Most rides will be community-led and rubberbanded (E cat) unless specified by the event pace category.

Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday.
01 - 7 June - Island Hopper
08 - 14 June - Hot Laps
15 - 21 June - Croissant
22 - 28 June - London Flat
29 & 30 June - Beach Island Loop

Sunday.
LGBTQz Ride with Pride club social ride.

Each Wednesday in June - Race with Pride in our fun and friendly crit format.
Each Saturday in June - Join us to Chase the Rainbows. Can you work together with others in your pace category to chase the rainbows in front, or keep the chasing rainbows at bay?

Pick up some exclusive rainbow swag with our different unlocks, including the chance to unlock vintage Pride On kits and socks on Throwback Thursdays!

Find out more about LGBTQ Zwifters at https://lgbtq-zwifters.com/

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

It's Crit time! Come and join in the fun on a number of multi-lap short routes. Get ready to dig deep and push to the finish line!

What is Racing Score?

Racing Score is an intuitive system that replaces the traditional categories (A - D) with a 0-1000 scale to reflect your current level, considering various metrics like race performances and power. This score helps Zwift recommend the most competitive band to race in, ensuring a fun, rewarding, and exciting experience as you track your progression throughout your Zwift racing adventures.

WHAT IS ZWIFT POWER? For further information on connecting to Zwift Power check out this support page: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/connecting-to-zwiftpower-SyldRc_4H

name: GXY HIGH STRATOSPHERE [2.3-2.7wkg] – CAT C
description:
Welcome to GXY High Stratosphere!
This ride is looking to help you to develop towards Category C and we call it our High Stratosphere (Cat C) group ride.

We will achieve this together by providing a consistent pace to help you build both your strength and stamina at the lower end of the Cat C range of power.

The ride leader and the team will bring you back down to Earth on 60 minutes whilst remaining within the advertised power range! (expect an approximate 2.5wkg ride average depending on body size and course selection) The event is designed to push Cat D's even further towards the next power category. Please respect the leader’s pace and watch your fitness develop!

GXY are a friendly and supportive club who strive to help others succeed their goals.

Our Club emphasis is based on inclusivity, diversity, respect and providing fun at all levels on Zwift whether riding socially, racing your legs off or hanging around our optional chat groups waiting for our IRL meet ups!

We are of course looking forward to riding with you.

If you want to become a member and join our community to race, ride socially, or both, please come and join ideally via our Facebook link:

name: The XP Express with Wobble Cycle Club
description:
All aboard The XP Express!

We're dishing out Double XP in this event so sign up, kit up and get ready to Level Up.

The XP Express is a turbocharged ride where every pedal stroke counts twice. Whether you're starting your Zwift journey or a seasoned pro, hop aboard to Level Up your ride.

How does it work?
The XP Express events will double your XP, helping you wrack up 40XP per kilometer or 64XP per mile! Leveling Up is the perfect way to unlock new swag, access to bikes and wheels, new routes and, of course, some bragging rights.

Use this event as an easy recovery ride, a quick warm up before your next race or push yourself to the limit to see how much XP you can earn.

name: Zwift Women's Training Club Workout
description:
Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! Get the most out of your Zwifting with training designed by world-class coaches, like 3x Olympic Gold medalist, Kristin Armstrong!

The group workouts will be held every 3 hours UTC on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We’ll also offer recovery rides every 3 hours on Wednesdays - be on the look out for special guests joining those! Our main goal is to provide you with a consistent experience week in and week out, to challenge yourself in a supportive group setting, making friends and getting fit along the way! 

Join the Zwift Women’s Training Club to connect with new ride friends, ask questions, and get advice from experts.  https://www.zwift.com/clubs/ZwiftWTC/join

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides every 3 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays in addition to the Tuesday/Thursday workouts.

Most groups will start slower and finish faster than the indicated pace. Feel free to mix in some intervals and race your friends. #pbt

name: Applewood Cycling Group Ride
description:
Established in September 2020, The Applewood Cycling Group Ride is surely one of the longest continually running weekly group rides on Zwift. Join leader Stephen Collins for a challenging B+ tempo training ride in the lavender fields of France covering two full laps of the Douce route. Our ride incorporates both a steady group with the leader targeting pulls on the front at 3.5 to 3.9 WKG (drafting average ~3.2wkg), and we offer an all-out A+ pace breakaway group. Our breakaway is fully sanctioned and an important element of our group ride dynamic. Every now and then the beacon group catches the break, but only very rarely. No fence, proud. No sweep. We do honor the finish line with a competitive sprint!

We encourage friendly group banter during the ride. Our goal is to create an outstanding training ride that is social and entertaining. Thanks to all our wonderful regulars and a big welcome to all newcomers.

name: Team DRAFT Thursday Race
description:
Welcome to the Thursday Race brought to you by Team DRAFT!
We encourage that all participants head over to zwiftpower.com and register. For more information see: https://zwiftinsider.com/zwiftpower-signup/ Riders who have not completed the Zwiftpower registration will not be included in the official race results. We also ask that your Zwift activities be saved publicly, and that you open and maintain a Strava account to allow for organizer analysis. Any rider exhibiting questionable performance during a the race may be disqualified.

RULES:
- No zPower riders.
- Heart rate monitors mandatory for all categories
- 5min and 20min CEVAZ limits apply. Riding in the wrong category will lead to disqualification.

RACE CATEGORIES:
A: 4.0 W/kg to 5.0 W/kg
B: 3.2 W/kg to 3.99 W/kg
C: 2.5 W/kg to 3.19 W/kg
D: Under 2.49 W/kg

description: Starting on Tuesday 22nd October at 06:30 MST, join RAAM World Record Holder Lucas Clarke for the Le Col SUB6 Endurance Series on Zwift. Whether you’re preparing for ultra-distance events like Race Across America (RAAM), Transcontinental and Mallorca 312, aiming for your first ultra or looking to refine your training, this series is your key to mastering endurance.

Our goal is to provide a platform for all to enjoy while increasing awareness about the USMES organization which is an endurance-based team of Activeduty military, veterans including friends and family. name: DBR Base Endurance Ride
description:
Join the Danish Bike Riders for an endurance workout that will boost your aerobic threshold and train your body to use fat as energy rather than quickly depleting your glycogen stores. Continual efforts will boost your race performance and endurance.

This ride will have a ride leader, but the point is that everyone rides at their own level.

Stay in the blue power zone (zone 2) for the duration of the workout. You will quickly form grupettos with people of your own fitness level.

To bring up the power graph, press G on your PC or Mac. Tap the screen and the graph icon for IOS and Android.

E category - But 1.0-5.0 W/kg avg.

Official site : Danish Bike Riders - https://www.facebook.com/DanishBikeRiders

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level.

For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift

#dbr

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

name: Hexa'Quiz Ride
description:
[FRANÇAIS]

l'appli Kahoot! Tous les 4/5 kilomètres, une question arrive. Celui qui
répond bien et vite gagne.

On organise également un classement mensuel pour ajouter un peu de piquant
à l'aventure.

Les questions portent sur divers aspects du cyclisme : les exploits des
professionnels, les différents types de vélos, l'univers virtuel de Zwift,
et tout ce qui touche de près ou de loin à cette passionnante discipline
sportive.

Venez vous amuser et défier vos amis ! Que le meilleur gagne ! C'est le
moment de montrer vos connaissances tout en pédalant !

[ENGLISH]
HEXA'Quiz Ride is a fun competition combining cycling and general
knowledge. You pedal quietly while answering questions on the Kahoot! app.
Every 4/5 kilometers, a question comes up. Whoever answers well and quickly
wins.

A monthly ranking is also organized to add a little spice to the adventure.

The questions focus on various aspects of cycling: the exploits of the
professionals, the different types of bikes, the virtual world of Zwift,
and anything else related to this exciting sport.

Come and have fun and challenge your friends! May the best man win! It's
time to show off your knowledge while you pedal!

name: SZR Group Workout by Thyr
description:
Ride with Mattias Thyr at Ovning.se in courtesy of SZR as he makes workouts for the one who cares and lets him.
Nudging the grit! The home of the unstructured GWOs. Here you got motivating rides together with friends. Skip plans, just a exercise your pixels in a group is good for you, both mentally and physically. Every 6th week we do a #maxtjuga (as we say in Sweden) or a the 20min FTP test together.

On his 8th years and +350 GWO:s he created and lead personally on Zwift. Come join and, "Aim for the stars!

• The workout is approximately 60 minutes long and can be done either fasted or fueled. I personally recommend lots of sugars.
• The goal is to explore and feel the differences between various fueling strategies.
• Remember to adjust your calorie intake to match your energy needs before during and after the session.
• This workout is based on a percentage of your FTP (Functional Threshold Power).
• Ensure your FTP is accurate and up-to-date for the best experience.
• If needed, perform an FTP Test a day before on Zwift prior the workout.
• Use the Zwift Companion App or the Page Up/Down keys on your computer to adjust the FTP bias by 10% up or 25% down, helping you dial in the effort level to suit your preferences.

The goal with an SZR Ride is to focus on the Group and keeping the Group together while having fun to make the time fly fast! You should aim to sit between the fence and the yellow / red beacon.
The ride tempo is shown next to the ride category, this is rider weight / gender dependant.
Note that the average is for the total ride! There might be variations above or under the average during the ride.
Please always follow ride leader instructions.

name: SZR Pick n Mix
description:
Please join the SZR Pick n Mix Team as we wind down on a Thursday evening and prepare for the weekend ahead.

The goal with an SZR Ride is to focus on the Group and keeping the Group together while having fun to make the time fly fast! You should aim to sit between the fence and the yellow / red beacon.

The ride tempo is shown next to the ride category, this is rider weight / gender dependant.

Note that the average is for the total ride! There will be variations over or under the average during the ride due to the terrain.

There may well be optional intervals lead by either the Red or Yellow beacon, but one beacon will remain at the ride pace for those not wanting to participate in the interval.

After climbs / descents we will try to focus on getting the back of the group together.

Please always follow ride leader instructions.

name: The XP Express with Hercules Running and Tri
description:
All aboard The XP Express!

We're dishing out Double XP in this event so sign up, kit up and get ready to Level Up.

The XP Express is a turbocharged ride where every pedal stroke counts twice. Whether you're starting your Zwift journey or a seasoned pro, hop aboard to Level Up your ride.

How does it work?
The XP Express events will double your XP, helping you wrack up 40XP per kilometer or 64XP per mile! Leveling Up is the perfect way to unlock new swag, access to bikes and wheels, new routes and, of course, some bragging rights.

Use this event as an easy recovery ride, a quick warm up before your next race or push yourself to the limit to see how much XP you can earn.

name: NPRC - Run Every Day Powered By NoblePro
description:
Come and join the fastest growing running club on Zwift.  With a choice of 5 or 10k you can pick your distance. Whether you are a beginner or experienced runner come and join us, you can run at whatever pace you like, it’s not a race unless you want it to be!

Each day is a different route and as new routes are released the courses will change to allow you to bag that badge.

You will run in our in game NPRC jersey and if you complete the event you get to keep it to wear wherever you like.

We also hold special events where you can win an actual jersey to wear in real life.

NPRC Facebook – We have a facebook group where you can join and talk about all things running.  Share your stories and get help and advice.

https://www.facebook.com/groups/1223724692417314/

NoblePro: - We are a team focused on elevating running through our treadmills and digital platforms. We create treadmills loved by runners and the wider running community for quality engineered hardware features and advanced software integration to give you the freedom to train with the apps you love.
https://www.noble-pro.com/

Kinni:- In a fitness world where treadmill bluetooth integration can be a confusing place, we aim to provide you with the ability to effortlessly connect. You can run structured treadmill workouts, connect and integrate with your favourite bluetooth fitness apps such as Zwift, Rouvy, Kinomaps and many more. We are focused on progress and advancement in integration, connectivity and control.

name: NoPinz R3R - Double Crit 2/2
description:
Welcome to this NoPinz R3R Race. The rules are simple....
Please use ZwiftPower's Minimum Category on your profile for race entry.
Cats A, and B will require a power source (power meter or smart trainer) and heart rate monitor.
Cat C will require power source (power meter or smart trainer) and heart rate monitor for podium spots.
Podium finishers in Cat A are expected to dual (power) record and to make analysis publicly available on ZwiftPower; they must also be using a direct drive trainer or power meter.
**Elite level performances are also expected to be supported by dual (power) recordings from reputable power sources or easily verifiable outside data. This applies to those with a history of such performances.
** 5.2 w/kg (20 mins); 6 w/kg (5 mins); 9.8 w/kg (1 min)
Zwift Activities must be saved publicly.
Please also maintain an open and active Strava profile to facilitate organiser inquiry.
Please see http://www.zwiftpower.com for finalised race results. The race is brought to you by NoPinz please visit https://nopinz.com/product-tag/subzero/ All subzero kit can be custom made in any design.

name: TSE POKER CHALLENGE 1/4
description:
TSE Poker Challenge: Virtual Cycling Competition
The TSE Poker Challenge is a virtual cycling competition organized by the TSE club, taking
place every Thursday. The event uses a "tiny" format, consisting of short mini-stages.

Calendar and Structure
The competition includes 4 events, each made up of 4 mini-stages lasting approximately 15
minutes each.

Race Times (Italian Time): 19:05, 19:25, 19:45, and 20:05.

Regulations and Technical Requirements
The event is open to categories A, B, C, and D with Category Enforcement active.
● Equipment: You may choose your preferred bike, but Time Trial (TT) bikes are
prohibited.
● Mandatory: A heart rate monitor is required; zPower is not allowed.
● Settings: Drafting and steering are enabled, while Powerups are disabled.
● Scoring: A dynamic system is used based on the number of participants (e.g., 60 starters
= 60 points for 1st place, 1 point for the last).
● Penalties: Athletes who change categories during the tour will receive penalties.

For technical support or team registrations, contact the organizers at 

Official Sites: * www.tsezwift.com * www.epicasport.com

name: PUMP: Loop Logic IV — Thursday (4 Laps)
description:
Same Distance. More Laps. Maximum Sass. ♥️🌶️

Welcome to Loop Logic, the weekday series where we prove that "going in circles" is actually a superpower. We’ve curated a week of routes that hit the 19–25km sweet spot with enough climbing to keep your glutes talking back to you.

The Logic is Simple:
We start with one big loop on Monday and add a lap every day until Friday. One lap is a warm-up, but five laps is a statement.

The PUMP Vibe:
Power in Numbers: No band here, ladies! This is your chance to find your rhythm, tuck into a friendly draft, and realize you’re much faster than you think.

Elevation is Our Love Language: Expect at least 100m of climb—just enough to feel the PUMP and earn that post-ride coffee.

Laughter > Watts: We ride hard, but we laugh harder. Whether you’re smashing a PR or just hanging onto a wheel for dear life, do it with a smile.

The Mission:
Show up for yourself, stay for the sisterhood, and let’s show exactly what women-powered logic looks like.

name: Team AMANI's Safari Ride
description:
Team AMANI's Safari Ride is an all category ride, organized by Team AMANI as a training and community engagement tool. Come train with the up and coming talent from East Africa!

Want to ride alongside some of the future stars of the gravel peloton? You've come to the right place! The routes may differ weekly and the rides will be periodically attended by the stars of  Team Amani as well as the future stars from our training facilities in Rwanda (Spoke Academy) and Kenya (the Amani House). We also welcome supporters of Team Amani to join and lead / take part.

So make sure to bring your A-game. There are 3 categories leaving from the start pen and everyone is able to sign-up according to their category and ride with the bunch. Challenge yourself on the segments we come across and make sure to set that PR!

Our goal is to stay as a group during the warming up, work hard at the climbs and regroup on the descents. We will break into a couple of different groups, so find your pace and grab a wheel. If you're feeling strong, pull a few friends across the flats to the hill.

So what is the AMANI Project? The AMANI project brings together initiatives aimed at enhancing access to the sport of cycling and creating opportunities for riders based in  East Africa. Our initiatives are:
- Team AMANI 
- Migration Gravel Race & Safari Gravel
- Amani House & Spoke Academy

Want to learn more or support the cause?

Follow us on our socials:

@teamamani
@spokeacademy

Check out:

https://www.teamamani.com/

name: CSPT club ride
description:
Welcome to CSPT; a cycling and running club with a difference. It's a place where members can meet up & have fun without any pressure to perform.

Whether you're short of motivation or inspiration then CSPT is the place for you. Drawing on years of experience from all walks of life and athletic experience we can help to motivate you to achieve whatever your goal is.

With CSPT - "YOU CAN"

This event has no leader, no fence and no rules because that's not what we're about. Stay with the bunch, often we are banded, we'll help you just enjoy being part of the club.

Please join our club : CSPT for further details.

name: Group Run 10k
description:
Join us for a 10k group run.   It's run-at-your-own-pace and all are welcome! 

Pick the closest pace group for you, but all groups will start together and you are free to fall back and run ahead. The pace groups designate average pace for the duration of the run. Most groups will start slower and finish faster than the indicated pace. Feel free to mix in some intervals and race your friends. #pbt

name: Stage 2: Level Up Racing: BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits
description:
Level Up Racing is June’s ZRacing monthly series. Race across five stages from June 1 to July 5, with a new route each week and up to 250 XP waiting at every banner. Complete stages to build series progress, chase the GC leaderboard, and grab bonus XP as you race.

Stage 2

Dates: June 8–14
Route: BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits
Laps: 1
Distance: 22.1 km
Elevation: 243 m

Stage 2 brings BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits, a punchier test with more elevation and more chances to keep building XP. One lap, one effort, and another shot to add to your series total.

MONTHLY GC COMPETITION

Looking for extra motivation? The Monthly GC (General Classification) Competition lets you track your progress across all stages. Each race counts—your times add up throughout the series, shaping the overall standings. At the end of the month, the fastest total time takes the win!

VIEW RESULTS: http://zwift.com/racing/leagues/zracingjun2026
—------------------
Zwift Racing Score is aimed at pairing you with riders of similar racing abilities to keep racing fun, fair, and competitive. Read the FAQ here: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/racing-score-faq-BkG9_Rqrh


ADVANCED CATEGORY = 650+
CATEGORY RANGE 1 = 0-159 | 160-269 | 270-389 | 390-509 | 510-649
CATEGORY RANGE 2 = 0-209 | 210-329 | 330-449 | 450-569 | 570-724

For riders with a Racing Score of 650 or higher, the' Advanced' category will have separate events scheduled every other hour.

Please note that in order to enter the Advanced category, you will need the following:
Heart Rate Monitor
Zwift Racing Score of over 650
Smart Trainer/Bike or Power Meter


Hourly ZRacing will be split into five tighter categories for more exciting competition. Plus, with hourly alternating category ranges, you’ll have more options to find races that suit your level.

name: ZTPL Cycling Club Coffee Ride
description:
☀️Weszliśmy w sezon wiosenno-letni.☀️
Część naszych eventów zostaje w kalendarzu, ale może zdarzyć się tak że nie będzie na nich naszych liderów jazd.
Jeśli tak się zdarzy, gorąca prośba do Was o jazdę wg. założeń danego eventu.
Nasze eventy i liderzy ZTPL Cycling Club wrócą ponownie na jesień 2026.
Póki co RIDE ON i korzystajcie z pogody, a jeśli nie możecie to bawcie się dobrze podczas naszych eventów.


Zapraszamy na wspólny event z ZTPL Cycling Club. Pamiętajcie o wyborze właściwej grupy.

Z założenia nasze jazdy prowadzą liderzy, którzy pomagają trzymać peleton w ryzach. Jeśli podczas eventu zabraknie lidera, starajcie się trzymać tempo na które się umówiliśmy w momencie gdy dołączyliście do wybranej grupy. To od Was zależy jak będziecie się bawić 😊
Po ukończonym evencie, jeśli jechaliście z nami pierwszy raz, w Waszym wirtualnym garażu będzie czekała nasza teamowa koszulka!
◾️Grupy jazdą w założonym tempie, które macie podane przy każdej z nich w momencie dołączenia.
◾️ Jeśli chcecie przejechać jazdę w tempie Coffee Ride wybierzcie o jedną grupę niżej niż sugeruje wam wasze FTP lub zwiftpower :)
◾️ Wartości podane w opisach dotyczą średniego tempa z CAŁEJ jazdy (nie uwzględniają interwałów, które mogą wystąpić podczas np. podjazdów)
◾️ PAMIĘTAJCIE że podczas jazd grupowych NIE UŻYWAMY ROWERÓW CZASOWYCH!
◾️ Starajcie się pilnować peletonu i nie zgubić koła, samemu bardzo trudno jest odrobić stratę.
◾️ Proszę słuchajcie poleceń lidera, które podczas jazdy wyświetlane są na środku ekranu.
◾️ Lider, który prowadzi grupę podświetlony jest na żółto.
◾️ Starajcie się jechać blisko lidera, starając się go nie wyprzedać i nie wyjeżdżać przed bramę, która informuje Was że jedziecie za szybko.
Proszę stosujcie się do poleceń lidera!
Szczególnie jeśli lider zauważy że grupa się porwała.

☀️We’re now in the spring and summer season.☀️
Some of our events will stay in the calendar, but there may be times when our ride leaders won’t be there. If that happens, we’d really appreciate it if you could still ride according to the plan of the event.
Our ZTPL Cycling Club events will be back in autumn 2026.
For now — RIDE ON, enjoy the good weather, and if you can’t, just have a great time at our events.

We would like to invite you to ZTPL Cycling Club Coffee Ride.
In order to ride with Coffee Ride pace, please choose your group wisely.

Our rides are usually led by leaders who help keep the peloton in check. If there is no leader during the event, try to stick to the pace we agreed on when you joined the selected group.
◾️Group E is for total beginners with easy pace at around 1.3-1.7 wk/g
◾️Group D is a beginner group. The pace is calm, we learn how to ride in a Zwift peleton with 1.8-2.5 w/kg pace
◾️Group C is between group D and more advanced Group B. Pace 2.7-3.2 w/kg.
Important: If your FTP is around 2.5w/kg, this group will not be for you

◾️Please listen to the leader’s commands which are displayed in yellow during the whole ride. The leader who leads the group is highlighted in yellow. Please don’t pass the leader.
◾️Please follow the leader instructions! Especially if the leader notices that the group has been swept away. The leader is highlighted in yellow.
◾️At the and wait for the leader’s command: GOGOGO and start your sprint. Enjoy!

◾️If you would like to get yourself our ZTPL Cycling Club team jersey please visit our shop https://inoni.cc/en/?s=ztpl&post_type=product
or you can order our Casual T-Shirt and Hoodies https://wintertal.com/en/133-ztplcc
