name: ZZRC Soft Spin 1.5 with Andi
description:
Welcome to our ZZRC Soft Spin 1.5 with Andi.  This is a group ride, not a race, where we encourage riding together.

Our rides are open to all riders, the category enforcement merely allows us to ensure a safe and quality ride for you the riders and for our group.

In 2015 ZZRC was founded and are one of the oldest established clubs on Zwift.

YELLOW BEACON will pace between 1.3-1.5. on the ride, with a possible increase of watts on inclines or sprints, but the average for the whole ride will be 1.5

We strongly promote group riding so on most of our rides we will use the Fence to help encourage that. Using a fence ensures that the ride is not over paced.

In the event of falling off the back of the main group, you will need to pace well over group pace to bridge the gap and catch.

This is where our awesome ZZRC sweeps and Ride Buddies will help you return to group using their draft. They will give you clear encouraging instructions to aid this process.

Our crew are a caring bunch who dedicated a lot of hours to this club, but want you to have the best ride experience on Zwift

You will be fully supported and encouraged throughout the ride by the Leader, Sweeps and Ride Buddies.

Our rides do not allow the use of TT Bikes as they do not draft and will require you to push harder on the ride, and in these instances our Sweeps will not be able to help you.

Mountain bikes operate very similarly, minimum draft so more watts (effort) will be required for the ride and any chase backs to group.

All our rides have a 30 minute late join feature which allows you to rejoin if you have technical issues or you find yourself out of the group in the early stages of the ride. Using this feature SHOULD teleport you back into the main group with our YELLOW BEACON.

We love to have a chat on our rides so join us on our dedicated discord channel

https://discord.gg/teHeHABDHc

TOP TIPS

Stay close to the ride leader (or just in front on climbs), don’t let a gap form and the elastic snap!

Stay away from the Fence – We don’t like to fry anyone

Most important of all… HAVE FUN AND ENJOY THE RIDE.

#zzrc

Don’t forget to join our ZZRC-We Pace Not Race Facebook page and our club on the companion app

name: Hotchillee Gain Train
description:
What is it?
Firstly, IT’S NOT A RACE but that doesn’t mean it’s an easy pace no-drop ride. It’s a paced “Category +” Hare and Hounds where you will be working predominately at the upper end of your category and hanging on for as long as you can in search of those gains.

What are the paces?
Paces are based on what the Ride Leader for each group will average and our leaders are pretty accurate - check on ZwiftPower afterwards.   Buffet Class (D+) Leader will average 2.4 w/kg (departs at 1830)
Second Class (C+) Leader average 3.1 w/kg (departs at 1834)
First Class (B+) Leader will average 3.7 w/kg (departs at 1836)

Please do not push the pace faster than this, it ruins it for everyone - respect your Ride Leader, do what they ask and don’t sandbag.

Will the groups catch each other?
Usually we aim for there to be a catch/merge in the final 5km or so but this does depend on the course.
If a merge does happen, stronger riders are encouraged to “upgrade” to the faster group and, if you’re struggling, you can also “downgrade” to a slower one.

What if I get dropped?
Suck it up, maybe find someone to spin home with and try to hang on a bit longer next week - just like a IRL chain-gang, that’s how you get stronger.

Can I push it at the end?
With about 3km to go, your Leader will give a Go! Go! Go! shout and then, if you want, you can empty the tank.

  What is Hotchillee?
Hotchillee is both an events company that organises some of the world's best cycling events and a cycling community. Check out the website for details of events, rides and to get involved www.hotchillee.com

name: ZLDR Progression Event
description:
Welcome to our ZLDR Progression Event. Today we’re going to do a progression run, which basically starts a run at a slower pace and finishes at a faster pace than you started. So we’ll get progressively faster with each split. Progression runs help us build our endurance base but with less stress on our bodies than a typical interval or tempo run. This can help reduce the risk of injury. Plus it helps break up the monotony in our training.

Progression running also will help teach you smarter pacing, starting conservatively so you don’t burn out too soon. It also will help train your body to get used to pushing harder at the end of a race.

This event will start with a 10 minute warm up followed by 4 x 5 mins splits. The first split will be at 10k pace and each split will be a stair step up at +2%. Finally we will cool down for 10 minutes. So let’s get those shoes laced up and ready to go!

ZLDR is a group of diverse people, from speed demons to walkers, from people just getting to their first 5k to ultra runners. We are here to support your on-foot dreams and help you develop your running/walking skills. We are a collective group of supportive and experienced runners and walkers who want to help you set and achieve new goals!

name: EVO CC Race Series
description:
CATEGORY ENFORCEMENT IS ENABLED FOR ALL EVO RACES!

What is Category Enforcement? 

Category Enforcement will prevent Zwifters from entering a category they are not eligible for.  Our goal is to increase fairness in racing.

HOW DOES IT WORK?

- Zwift checks a racer's past performance using VO2 max and FTP to determine their race category.
- Racers can join a category at or above their category. For example, if you are "C" category, you can race in C, B, or A category. You will not be able to race in the D category and the option to join will be absent.

Welcome to EVO CC race series.  Start fast, hang on in the middle, then sprint for the win at the finish. Expect to push your heart rate to its maximum. Sprinkle a few of these into your training plan and watch your fitness grow.

To make racing as fair as possible we have enforced a few minor rules that will result in automatic disqualification on ZwiftPower.

All riders must wear a heart rate monitor
Riding in an incorrect category.

zPower riders will be disqualified in A, B, and C Podium. zPower is allowed in the D category. Race details and final results will be available at www.zwiftpower.com

#evo

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

name: FAAST CREW CHAIN GANG!
description:
COME JOIN THE CREW! https://taplink.cc/faastcrew
.
FAAST CREW GROUP RIDES! 🤘
Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday Zwift rides! Everyone is welcome to join… let’s have some fun and get them GAINZ!
.
TUESDAY FTP BUILDER! @ 18:45(gmt)
It’s time to put the work in… each week we will be aiming to push your limits with a workout aimed to boost those FTP numbers…
Come get involved and watch yourself get stronger each week.
.
WEDNESDAY SOCIAL RIDE! @ 18:45(gmt)
Social pace night (banded together)
The main aim of these rides will be to keep things easy and sociable… not only to allow for a wider range of capabilities to get involved… but if you’re looking to get stuck in on Thursdays ride, have yourself an active rest day and use this ride to get to know your riding buddies.
There will also be some “optional” watt bombs being dropped… get involved if you fancy some sprint training!
.
THURSDAY CHAIN GANG! @ 18:45(gmt)
Chain gang night (around 4w/kg)
Come get stuck in and let’s empty those tanks!
This will be a full gas effort… we work as a unit for the most part, let’s try keep things together and help keep the pack strong… and we will operate a sweeper up until the half way mark.
There will however be a sprint finish with results, so the last 5-10minutes it’s every man/woman for themselves. Get stuck in and try take the glory.
This will be a race format but the finish line is an imaginary one as the clock hits zero.
.
LATE JOIN is enabled, so you can join us up to 30 mins after the start time, with the event link.
.
Please help spread the word, invite your pals and be sure to tag us in anything you post… we like to see you suffering, so post on your story of you smashing those pedals and tag @faastcrew.
.
PLEASE JOIN OUR ZWIFT CLUB.
That’s where all the rides will be posted but if you happen to miss them make sure to follow our Instagram page and keep up to date with any upcoming events and announcements.
(All relevant links, click the tap link in bio)
.
We look forward to seeing you all there, come get involved and LET’S HAVE IT!
.
The FAAST CREW.

name: DBR Thursday Race
description:
Welcome to DBR Thursday Race.
All will start with 1 minute between RS categories. Expect each race to be highly competitive and have fun.
Categories
Each race will be using Zwift Racing Score (ZRS) for categorization.
race up a category, if your RS is at the top end of a category. Or if you simply desire an added challenge.
- A: 1000 =< 690
- B:690<520
- C:520<350
- D:350<180
- E:180<=0
Your Zwift Racing Score is determined by how much success you have in races.
better against people with higher ZRS, then your ZRS may increase. If you place worse than people with lower ZRS, then your score might decrease. Read more about ZRS here - https://support.zwift.com/en_us/racing-score-faq-BkG9_Rqrh <https://support.zwift.com/en_us/racing-score-faq-BkG9_Rqrh>
If your ZRS increases past a category boundary during the series, your points earned will not transfer to the new category with you.
RULES:
Smart trainer or power meter is required. zPower will be removed.
Heart rate monitors are compulsory for all categories.
No TT bikes unless it's a TT event.
You need to have a registered account with Zwiftpower.com and accept their terms and conditions to be in the results of the race.
Misc.
Race organizers may request riders in all categories to provide a dual recording or a matching RL effort (Strava) in order to verify a Zwift race effort. Failure to comply may result in disqualification from the event. Failure to provide a dual recording or RL effort on three requests may result in disqualification from future events, until a dual recording with a matching effort is provided.
Race organizers may exclude a rider from the results, due to poor sportsmanship. Examples may be bad language, sandbagging or other behavior of a disruptive manner.

name: Poursuite de la Lanterne Rouge p/b Velos
description:
Looking for a fun and well supported social ride that will make you stronger? Then join us on Poursuite de la Lanterne Rouge! This event is great for confident D riders looking to step up to something a bit faster, as well as experienced riders who want to test themselves at race pace. We ride together for 45 minutes at 23mph/38kph (2.3w/kg), have a KOM to conquer then a Sprint to warm the legs, then we unleash our Red Beacon to step on the gas and - after a little head start to give our Lanterne Rouge a fighting chance - anyone game for a chase is free to fly. Three chase groups are offered with 3-6 minute deficits to close, and you are guaranteed to get stronger with each attempt to catch! The Yellow Beacon leader will continue at the listed pace the full hour to help those who don’t fancy a chase finish in friendly company. Strong sweep support is available for anyone needing a wheel get back into the leader’s group.
Join our social group at: www.teamvelos.co.uk

name: UK Armed Forces Cycling Community Race Night
description:
We are back being "in the chop" is an Aussie expression that you won't read about in the UCI rulebook. It's one of the many nuances of bike racing that only comes with experience.

Sometimes when you're in a race and find yourself in the final break-away bunch you might get asked "are we in the chop?" or "are we chopping it?". This is referring to collusion between the lead riders to work together until the finish. Many times a break-away will be doomed in the final kilometres because everyone starts playing cat and mouse, attacking, sitting up, etc.

But all that goes out the window in the last lap. This is generally where the group comes together and the final push begins. Working together goes out the window and is every man or woman for themselves for the final sprint to the line.

The Chop is a flat fast time-based handicap race. Do you always get blown out the back on the start of a multi grade race trying to hang onto the guy going with A grade pushing 5w/kg. Well not on The Chop. Released in Grades there are time splits from D to A with the intention of all coming together at the end for the big finish. Each Grade wears a different Zwift kit making each grade easily identifiable on who's wheel you want to catch if they go past.

Races happen on Tuesday evenings. We plan to add further races in the future. No single race has been the same. Many variables are at play on The Chop including course (which is generally a flat course), race numbers, and the inevitable sandbaggers. It has been called a team time trail and cat and mouse but the real racers know it only as "THE CHOP". Do you have what it takes to take the glory?

New to running, coming back after some time off, or simply want a nice warm up or cool down session? Join us as we spend 30 minutes moving the legs in this slow-paced, social event. The goal of the event is to encourage folks to move.

name: RollCo: The Ascent
description:
⛰️ Your ascent. Rise together.

What is The Ascent?
The Ascent is Rolling Collective’s weekly climbing-focused ride, built around shared effort and individual pacing. It’s a space to work through long climbs alongside others, drawing motivation from the group while riding your own line to the top.

The Ride:
Each week focuses on sustained climbing and elevation. Every other week, The Ascent takes on Alpe du Zwift, giving riders the opportunity to work toward the 25× Alpe Climb achievement as part of a regular, supported routine.

Pacing & Expectations:
Riders are encouraged to climb at their own pace, managing effort and intensity individually. Expect company on the road, encouragement in the chat, and the shared satisfaction of finishing together, wherever that may be on the climb. If you’re looking for a pacer, they can often be found on our discord or club chat.

Why Join Rolling Collective?
All RollCo events are open for any rider, club or non-club, we don’t care who you ride for, just that you’re here for the roll! We’re more than a club — we’re a global community of riders who support each other, grow together, and celebrate every ride, whether it’s a grind, a badge hunt, or a race. Join us on Discord, connect with fellow riders, and be part of something bigger.

Forward, Together

name: EVO CC Sprint Race Series
description:
CATEGORY ENFORCEMENT IS ENABLED FOR ALL EVO RACES!

What is Category Enforcement? 

Category Enforcement will prevent Zwifters from entering a category they are not eligible for.  Our goal is to increase fairness in racing.

HOW DOES IT WORK?

- Zwift checks a racer's past performance using VO2 max and FTP to determine their race category.
- Racers can join a category at or above their category. For example, if you are "C" category, you can race in C, B, or A category. You will not be able to race in the D category and the option to join will be absent.

Welcome to EVO sprintrace series. Shorter more compact races for the rider looking for an effective high intensity race. Start fast, hang on in the middle, then sprint for the win at the finish. Expect to push your heart rate to its maximum. Sprinkle a few of these into your training plan and watch your fitness grow.

To make racing as fair as possible we have enforced a few minor rules that will result in automatic disqualification on ZwiftPower.

All riders must wear a heart rate monitor
Riding in an incorrect category.

zPower riders will be disqualified in A, B, and C Podium. zPower is allowed in the D category. Race details and final results will be available at www.zwiftpower.com

#evo

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

name: GGCC Glasgow Green Cycle Club Thursday Training Ride
description:
GGCC group rides are TRAINING events, category C, with a yellow beacon leader. The beacon leader will ride to 2.5w/kg pace average wherever possible.

Please look out for our training rides 3 days a week, every week - Tuesdays at 20.45 UTC, Thursdays at 21.00 UTC and Saturdays at 11.30am UTC. Use #ggcc to search, as in https://zwift.com/events/tag/ggcc

The Glasgow Green Cycle Club (GGCC) training rides are intended to provide a challenge for riders, and are open to all timezones. You should ride as a group, following the instructions of the beacon ride leader(s) for any sprints, intervals and spicy segments, regrouping after each when requested. All our group rides also have a closing minirace, to start from behind the beacon.

GGCC is a Glasgow based cycling club whose “in real life” (irl) club runs and training rides are always organized into pace groups, which match the Zwift categories quite well. GGCC also has a good race pedigree and presence in Scotland, and so we have organized this training ride series to suit what we believe is relevant to bike riders’ interests in performance and improvement in our club, in other Glasgow clubs, in Scotland and the UK. Racers will, no doubt, aspire to try our other events, both our Monday 20.10 UTC Zwift races, and our Friday 19.45 UTC TTs.

As we expect our club’s riders to be able to ride 50 miles at a 15mph average on our Sunday rides, such steady riding members will be comfortable with Zwift Category C, and in our various rides we cater for all abilities, through the Zwift ABCD levels. Beacon leaders communicate via Zwift messaging (always) and/or Discord (sometimes) to vary the pace to allow for sprints, intervals, and optionally a mini-race towards the end of the rides, with regrouping after each segment. Make as much use of drafting as you can, for more effective sprinting and intervals.

Results can be seen at the end of the ride on screen, and we will, in common with many other ride series, publish your results on zwiftpower.com too, based on each category.

All bikes and PUs are allowed, but better not to use TT bikes (which don’t draft) on our group rides and races. Please add GGCC (X) to your Zwift name to allow your ride presence to be recognized, where X is your desired ride category. Categories are related to your Functional Threshold Power (FTP); use your FTP and then divide by your weight in kg, then pick the correct ride and group.

C: 2 W/kg to 3 W/kg FTP; the beacon leader will ride to 2.5w/kg pace average.

PLEASE NOTE: Strava data for our rides must be open (not private or hidden). Please use a heart monitor so that we can monitor correlated power and heart rate to help assure fair riding.
You can use our Discord channel to talk to each other at https://discord.gg/UDhdEQA
Please see the GGCC Zwift page link at http://www.glasgowgreencycleclub.co.uk/ for more.

For more about specific Zwift courses for our events, see the Zwift Companion schedule, and also https://zwiftinsider.com/ where there is a wealth of information about all things Zwift.

Cat C - 2.5 - 3.2 w/kg (min 150W)

description:
The Move for Lex workout honors avid Zwifter and cyclist Alexa Leary, who was seriously injured in a bike crash in July 2021.

The #moveforlex movement is all about moving for those who can't and we'd love to see a huge group moving for Lex here every Friday for a workout.

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

name: AATC Thursday Interval Workout
description:
WORKOUT DESIGNER

Matt Dana of the Ann Arbor Triathlon Club - Group workouts make training so much more fun. The Ann Arbor Triathlon Club promotes the sport of triathlon in Southeast Michigan. We have all levels of Triathletes.  

ABOUT GROUP WORKOUTS

Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normal event and once the event starts, workout mode begins. Everyone stays together regardless of power output. That's right, if you're outputting 100W and another Zwifter is outputting 400W you will stay in exactly the same position relative to each other. Only if you stop pedaling and fall 6 meters behind the group will the rubber-banding stop.

HELPFUL HINT

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level. 

For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift

name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 27
description:
WTRL Team Time Trial #373

Our weekly WTRL Team Time Trial (TTT) allows teams of 3-8 Zwifters to race against the clock together throughout the day to achieve the fastest possible times. Teams are arranged into WTRL's unique Coffee Classes and feature both women's only Coffee Classes and mixed gender too.
  
 There are 30 racing events and teams can be registered up 30 minutes before each race event starts at www.wtrl.racing/ttt-home/ and you can pick your start time from the available slots. Each team is issued a unique RacePass that must be clicked by each team member to gain access to the event for sign-up. You'll also be able to check out the rules, course records and results which update live throughout the day.
  
 Teams & Riders must be registered with www.WTRL.racing and you'll need to be sharing data, via your Zwift Profile Connections with www.zwiftpower.com.
  
 If you are looking for a team, head to our dedicated WTRL TTT Facebook page where plenty of teams are always happy to welcome guest riders and new team mates (https://www.facebook.com/groups/WTRLTTT). Not on Facebook? Feel free to drop us an email with your preferred WTRL TTT Zone and current Zwift Category 
  
 #wtrl #wtrlttt

name: Faster Masters A/B/C Team Pursuit
description:
Thursdays’ Team Pursuit includes three teams starting at different times. Team C will start first followed by Team B, with Team A departing last. The goal is for the faster teams behind to catch Team C during the ride while all three teams hold their respective advertised paces. Starting time gaps may be adjusted during the season to maintain the ride concept, that being: as faster teams catch the team(s) in front, the catch will offer riders in a slower group who wish to increase their effort to do so by joining the faster team as they pass. Additionally, the catch offers riders in the faster team(s) the opportunity to jump in with the slower team(s) and recover to the finish. Riders who jump onto a faster team may realize they cannot hold the pace have an option to fall back to their starting group and try the same the next week to see if they can hold on longer. This is a great way to get stronger riding in a team format. 

All rides include a 30-minute Late Join period. During this time, dropped riders can use Late Join to rejoin their team. If you find that the team you selected is either too fast or too slow for your pace, you can switch teams within the first 30 minutes of the start time of the team you would like to join by using Late Join. 

We do not sweep during the first 30 minutes of a ride. If you fall behind for any reason during this time, we recommend using Late Join. We usually do not have designated sweepers (Red Beacon). After the first 30 minutes, if you get dropped and want to rejoin your team, please send a message in the format HELP(X), where X is the number of seconds you are off the back (for example, HELP5). If you reach out early, one or more stronger riders may come to assist you. If a sweep is needed we recommend you message help within 10 seconds.

We look forward to having you join us. The team pursuit is an excellent endurance and strength building adventure. 

Connect with Faster Masters on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/groups/2286721591625605

name: RO4H "Aaahh, Thursday!" Social Ride
description:
Welcome to the RO4H “Aaahh, Thursday!” Social Ride.

The RO4H “Aaahh, Thursday!” Social Ride is a social group ride hosted by the Ride On 4 Health community. We foster a friendly, casual, supportive, and respectful atmosphere that embraces everyone from the most seasoned Zwifter to the first-time group ride participant.

The pace varies depending on the terrain, but the ride will have an overall average pace of around 18–20 MPH (27–32 KPH). The pace on the flats sections will be slightly faster in the peloton and be sub 2 W/KG on climbs. We typically ride mostly flat routes with only a few short hills, if any. Sometimes we take on some slightly hillier routes for variety, but most of our rides will be gently rolling to flat terrain.

We try to be a no-drop ride, but ultimately, this pace is a recovery pace for some and a great effort for others. You should be prepared to meet the average pace and strive to stay in the ride leader's peloton to benefit from the group draft effect. Being a social ride, we don’t chase flyers — but flyers are free to fly. The “Aaahh, Thursday!” Social Ride is certainly not a race.

Sweepers are available to assist those off the back. We do not want anyone to ride alone unless they choose. The sweepers will variably help riders bridge to the leader's peloton or form a second pace group. We do not want riders to ride alone unless they want to.

Join us for the RO4H “Aaahh, Thursday!” Social Ride —you'll almost certainly break a sweat, hear a few dad jokes, and might even have fun.

View the RO4H ride schedule: https://www.zwift.com/events/tag/ro4h

Look us up on FB: https://www.facebook.com/groups/ZwiftRideOn4Health/

#ro4h

name: Zwift Women's Training Club Workout
description:
Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! Get the most out of your Zwifting with training designed by world-class coaches, like 3x Olympic Gold medalist, Kristin Armstrong!

The group workouts will be held every 3 hours UTC on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We’ll also offer recovery rides every 3 hours on Wednesdays - be on the look out for special guests joining those! Our main goal is to provide you with a consistent experience week in and week out, to challenge yourself in a supportive group setting, making friends and getting fit along the way! 

Join the Zwift Women’s Training Club to connect with new ride friends, ask questions, and get advice from experts.  https://www.zwift.com/clubs/ZwiftWTC/join

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides every 3 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays in addition to the Tuesday/Thursday workouts.

description:

Some may have a higher WKG up front pulling the band, you are welcome as well. Get a burn in those legs!!!!! We also have a sweep team at your disposal in case you fall out of the band. We are not racers but conquerors, an inclusive and dedicated group striving to help riders achieve their goals through teamwork, friendships and most of all unwavering support. Our rides are about the journey. We have a special bond with all those who join. We expect everyone to be treated with respect. Empathy and tolerance are appreciated as others will have differing views. Stay focused on what unites us: cycling and Zwift. Practice kindness. Please join our team every Thursday!

For more information on all our weekly events, join our club Phoenix Rising on Zwift Companion.

name: Zwift Crit Racing Club - Downtown Dolphin
description:
It's Crit time! Come and join in the fun on a number of multi-lap short routes. Get ready to dig deep and push to the finish line!

What is Racing Score?

Racing Score is an intuitive system that replaces the traditional categories (A - D) with a 0-1000 scale to reflect your current level, considering various metrics like race performances and power. This score helps Zwift recommend the most competitive band to race in, ensuring a fun, rewarding, and exciting experience as you track your progression throughout your Zwift racing adventures.

WHAT IS ZWIFT POWER? For further information on connecting to Zwift Power check out this support page: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/connecting-to-zwiftpower-SyldRc_4H

Please note; for your results to show up in Zwift Power you must be using a Heart Rate Monitor (HRM) and be riding on a smart trainer, smart bike, or using a power meter.

name: USMeS - Movement Drill (D) 1.8 - 2.2w/kg
description:
Welcome to USMeS Movement Drill - 1.8 - 2.2
This session is a step up and designed to prepare you for Force Development immediately following. The focus is on coordinated movement, controlled pressure, and working together while the intensity nudges a tad higher.
✅ Pace: an average of 1.8–2.2 w/kg
✅ Duration: 55 minutes
While we aim for an overall ~2.1w/kg average, ( 'ISH ), we do push on climbs, and sprints WILL be encouraged. When the pace lifts, make your move, then fall back in quickly and keep the group intact.
Ride sharp, respect the leader, and protect the group.
This is where we wake things up.
Move well now. Be ready to apply what you've learned, @Force Development, next.
#conqueringlimits
#challengeaccepted

name: KRG Thursday Night Crit
description:
While we are all stuck at home, please join us in the virtual edition of Fair Park Crits, a mainstay of DFW cycling.

We are NOT using standard Zwift categories, and also having a women's only race. If you are a usual nighter racer you know where to sign-up, but if you're joining us virtually:

As and Bs into the "A" category. This is a "P/1/2/3" field. 

Zwift Cs into "B". This is a "3/4" race. 

Ds and beginner racers please choose "C". AKA the 4/5 or novice race. 

Ladies, you can choose your correct field above or race the women's only, up to you! 

If you race the A race irl, you may find yourself not quite fitting into the pace of a Zwift A field. If that's the case do an FTP test, make sure your weight is up to date and let us know so we can look at revisiting the categories. 

For more info join us on Facebook at https://www.facebook.com/fairparkcrits/

name: The HERD Thirsty Thursday
description:
The Herd's Thirsty Thursday (THTT) Dual Pace Social Group Ride

This group ride offers a dual pace in a social environment. The goal is to keep our rides entertaining with games and trivia, educational with Zwift tips, and on pace. This ride offer our traditional Cat “D” option or a slightly higher paced Cat “C” option.

Our ride leaders’ goal is to keep to the advertised pace, averaged over the course of the ride. However, bear in mind that there are situations such as incline and descents that will affect the pace. To this, we ask that you pay attention to the rider leader announcements and adjust your pace accordingly. Stay close to the yellow beacon where the draft is most effective. As is customary to all Herd rides, we offer full Yellow (Ride Leader) and Red beacon (Sweeps) support.

If you find yourself wanting more of a challenge, we encourage you to join our sweep team as they ride “sweep-tervals” (above advertised pace) to help bring riders back to the ride leader.

Riding alone is not an option, as Herd rides are geared to be inclusive and fun.

#herd

name: Run in the Park Summer Run League - Week 2
description:
Results, FAQ's and a link to the Run in the Park Facebook group at www.runinthepark.co.uk  

Please enter the category that aligns with your personal best 5km finish time. There will be an element of flexibility to allow for sprint finishes or small improvements, but runners consistently entering a category below their ability may be moved to the appropriate category or disqualified from the league standings.

The groups are based on Zwift guidelines as shown in the event description, either on the website or on the ZCA, and are detailed below:

Group A - 5km finish time of less than 22:20 or an average pace quicker than 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile)
Group B - 5km finish time of between 22:21 and 25:00 or an average pace of between 4:29 min/km (7:12 min/mile) and 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile)
Group C - 5km finish time of between 25:01 and 28:51 or an average pace of between 5:00 min/km (8:03 min/mile) and 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)
Group D - 5km finish time of 28:52 or slower, or an average pace slower than 5:46 min/km (9:17 min/mile)

Points will be awarded based on finishing position within each category, using the fastest times across all events on the day.
1st place will receive 100 points, 2nd place 98 points, 3rd place 96 points, 4th place 95 points, and 5th place 94 points. Points will then continue to reduce by 2 points per position from 6th place onwards.

All finishers will receive points.

name: USMeS - Force Development - Early - 2.2 - 2.8w/kg

Welcome to USMeS - Force Development - Early - 2.2 - 2.8w/kg
This is a spicier C ride designed to build power, test your legs, and keep the group together. Expect controlled intensity, climbs that push you, and spots to spice things up and make the ride more fun.
✅ Pace: an average of 2.2–2.8 w/kg
✅ Duration: 60 minutes
We aim for an overall ~2.5 w/kg average, we do push on climbs, and when the pace lifts, go for it, then fall back in quickly and ride as a unit.
Ride sharp. Respect the leader. Protect the group. This is where we develop force, together.
Push hard. Ride together.

description:
Join Stephen Cousins and NoblePro for a 500 metre climb. Set your treadmill to 12% incline and run 4.2km of distance to reach 500 metres elevation. If your treadmill doesn't go that high, set it as high as it will go and join us anyway!

"He who would learn to fly one day must first learn to stand and walk and run and climb and dance; one cannot fly into flying.” Friedrich Nietzsche
https://www.brainyquote.com/quotes/friedrich_nietzsche_159166

#fear

name: BMC/Walmart Cycling Club Social
description:
Join the BMC/Walmart Cycling Club for a spirited group ride on this frozen arctic-blast night! (For much of the USA, at least) This is a social ride, with some spice. It is all about fun. Feel free to fly but it is more fun to ride together. Beacon will maintain prescribed pace with the potential for a few spicy moments. Sweepers will be back. All will be keeping the good vibes strong!
The BMC / Walmart Cycling Team was born to promote fitness through cycling in NWA. We are a group of enthusiasts cyclists and professional racers participating in all the different disciplines cycling has to offer. BMC is a cycling club located in and around Northwest Arkansas formed in 1979 by among others, the late Joe Martin. We are roadies, mountain bikers, tandem riders, tri-athletes, unicyclists, etc. We ride bicycles and that’s our “community”. Visit http://www.ridebmc.com to learn more or to join the club!

name: ZLDR Mid-Week Long Run
description:
Welcome to the ZLDR 21.1k Mid-Week Long Run. Whether you come for 3k, 5k, 10k or the full distance we are here to support your running dreams and help you develop your running skills. We are a collective group of supportive and experienced runners who will do our best to help you reach your goals.

Whether you’re speeding across the roads of Makuri or taking a gentle jog, join us for whatever distance but keep joining us and we can help you get to 21.1k and beyond. It’s always easier to run with others.

Not everyone gets the weekend off. For those of us who give our lives over to work on the weekends, please join us every week for your mid-week long run!

We’ve got 21.1km (13.1 miles) set aside just for you! Run as little or as much as you’d like, feel free to run more, to work in your interval training, to ease in a few recovery miles…. Whatever your mid-week goal may be, we’re here to help make it possible!

As with any of our runs, you are not required to go the entire distance listed. But we are a distance running group and would like to offer our members a chance every week to put their legs to the test and see how far they can go.

Hope to see you there!

ZLDR is a group of diverse people, from speed demons to walkers, from people just getting to their first 5k to ultra runners. We are here to support your running dreams and help you develop your running skills. We are a collective group of supportive and experienced runners and walkers who want to help you set and achieve new goals!

description:

The XP Express is a turbocharged ride where every pedal stroke counts twice. Whether you're starting your Zwift journey or a seasoned pro, hop aboard to Level Up your ride.

Stage 2

name: Zwift Women's Training Club Workout
description:
Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! Get the most out of your Zwifting with training designed by world-class coaches, like 3x Olympic Gold medalist, Kristin Armstrong!

The group workouts will be held every 3 hours UTC on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We’ll also offer recovery rides every 3 hours on Wednesdays - be on the look out for special guests joining those! Our main goal is to provide you with a consistent experience week in and week out, to challenge yourself in a supportive group setting, making friends and getting fit along the way! 

Join the Zwift Women’s Training Club to connect with new ride friends, ask questions, and get advice from experts.  https://www.zwift.com/clubs/ZwiftWTC/join

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides every 3 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays in addition to the Tuesday/Thursday workouts.

name: USMeS - Force Development - Late - 2.2 - 2.8w/kg
description:
Welcome to USMeS - Force Development - Late - 2.2 - 2.8w/kg

This is a spicier C ride designed to build power, test your legs, and keep the group together. Expect controlled intensity, climbs that push you, and spots to spice things up and make the ride more fun.
✅ Pace: an average of 2.2–2.8 w/kg
✅ Duration: 60 minutes
We aim for an overall ~2.5 w/kg average, we do push on climbs, and when the pace lifts, go for it, then fall back in quickly and ride as a unit.
Ride sharp. Respect the leader. Protect the group. This is where we develop force, together.
Push hard. Ride together.
#conqueringlimits
#challengeaccepted

name: "Russian Step - Hamster Style"
description:
“Russian Step - Hamster Style” is a cadence game where your legs spin like a hamster wheel! Alternate between high-speed spins (100–120 RPM) and controlled strength efforts (60–75 RPM). It builds coordination, pedaling efficiency, and muscle activation. Stay focused and flow with the rhythm. Let’s spin like warriors!
The “Russian Step - Hamster Style” workout is perfect for those aiming to improve cadence agility, pedaling efficiency, and neuromuscular responsiveness. By alternating very high RPM efforts with slower, strength-focused segments, it trains your body to handle sudden changes in rhythm and builds muscular coordination. It’s an excellent session for riders of all levels who want to break routine, sharpen their pedal stroke, and have fun while training. It also keeps the mind engaged and legs responsive.
⸻

        •        Warm-up (10 min):
        •        Easy spin at 90 RPM, gradually increasing power to 60% FTP.
        •        Main set (45 min):
        •        6 x (6 min intervals):
        •        1 min @ 80% FTP, 65 RPM
        •        1 min @ 95% FTP, 90 RPM
        •        30 sec @ 110 RPM, 70% FTP
        •        30 sec @ 60 RPM, 90% FTP
        •        1 min @ 100 RPM, 75% FTP
        •        1 min recovery @ 50% FTP, 85 RPM
        •        Finale (5 min):
        •        Progressive cadence ramp: start at 85 RPM, increase 5 RPM every minute
        •        Cool-down (10 min):
        •        Easy spin at 60% FTP, 85 RPM

name: FRR Weekend Warrior Series - ITT
description:
Flamme Rouge Racing are excited to bring you our WEEKEND WARRIOR which build on the Classica races and the full series to mid August.

Each event will offer 3 races Friday to Sunday, using three formats - iTT / Scratch / Points - each race will convert to points, based on segments and finish - a riders points total will be drawn from all 3 races, do more, score more!

Each event will center around the type of course and terrain of the monument, with the actual race day event being of a length that is fitting for the monument.

Classica races are part of the FRR Weekend Warrior Race Series for which there will be at least 10 WW events, refer to website for the Schedule and rules:

Series Schedule
https://flammerougeracing.com/race-schedule/

Rules
https://flammerougeracing.com/race-rules

Event Basics
- Public events - MIXED RACING
- Five Max 30day ZRS ranged pens
- Mandatory racing experience - HRM - Smart Trainers


- Season long Order of Merit (OoM)
- Best 7 scoring events to count (an event counts the points from all 3 races over

FRR Registered riders form the OoM - Top 10 earn prizes on condition they are FRR Subscribers 

For all details, registration and how to become an FRR subscriber vist our website:
https://flammerougeracing.com/

Primary Communication via DISCORD

Discord - RACE channel for questions, updates and lively chat - it is by far the best place to clarify or report anything during the series

Invite link: https://discord.com/invite/nQNWHQK6PS

Smart Trainers - HRM
- Smart Trainers are mandatory
- Race Control can verify with the Zwift platform 
- HRMs are mandatory

So be SMART and use a SMART trainer as your PRIMARY power source where you can....

FRR Code of Conduct
- We expect the best racing behavior from all riders, if riders have an issue then always contact race control via email first, we will investigate every request raised.
- In race we do not expect riders to abuse others, flag, report to race control, screen shot etc.... riders who ignore this will be DQ'd for the season
- Discord chat remains objective and banter - anything more will be removed and warnings/bans will be issued

And finally remember we all do this for fun and exercise so ride on and enjoy the FRR events....stay safe and if it starts to hurt then welcome to the fun zone...! 
(But stop if it really does hurt too much please!)

name: 3R VOLT Interval Ride [~2.6-3.2 w/kg avg]
description:
This is a 3R Group Ride so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong, please help the keeper beacon (Red) to assist other riders back to the pack. 3R VOLT runs five days a week and is designed to provide a solid and fun training platform for riders.

Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.8-3.2 w/kg.

The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides and training needs, the following is a typical week:
Monday – After what has hopefully been a fun backed weekend on the bike, this our recovery session
Tuesday – Tends to be more of a classic interval session, riders usually finish with an average of around 3.0w/kg
Wednesday – We take to the hills and one of our tougher sessions with riders averaging around 3.2w/kg
Thursday – is our no red beacon ride and again tough interval sets and riders finishing around 3.2w/kg
Friday - is a little different, we don't take ourselves too seriously and often play a variety of games and quizzes along side the intervals and riders end up with around 2.8-3.0w/kg

The rides are typically around an hour long, but some may take up to 75mins with the majority finishing with either a ramp or a mini race.

The group welcomes rider interaction through messaging and the VOLT discord server and features a friendly bunch of regulars to which newcomers, and riders stepping up from lower intensity rides, are always welcome. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/

This group ride is not a race so. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #Ride3R #RideRaceRaise.

Mondays and Tuesdays are our entry-level steady-state rides, where we aim to hold a steady 2.0-2.2 throughout. Wednesdays are a steady recovery ride, where we split into two different ability groups. Thursdays and Fridays are our interval sessions, designed to help Cat D riders push themselves a little further. For interval sessions we aim to average between 2.2-2.5 for the session, but there will be times above and below. Thursday and Friday sessions often include an optional mini-race at the end. Rides are typically around an hour long. Spark is a great introduction to group rides on Zwift, we are a friendly and supportive group who love to see one another succeed. We always have a sweeper (red beacon) whose wheel you can grab if you get dropped. There’s always plenty of good chat, via in-ride messages or on Discord. Come and join us! Join the 3R Facebook group for more info: https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #3R #RideRaceRaise

name: Watopia Dawn Patrol
description:
Welcome to Watopia Dawn Patrol hosted by Oslo Dawn Patrol.

The Dawn Patrol rides are an early morning social workout spin originating in Oslo, Norway that has since been adopted by local riders in several cities across the country and Europe. While a core group of riders braces the elements outdoors all year round, many of us take to the indoors during the winter season, bringing Watopia Dawn Patrol to life.

We head out for a ~60 min pre-work spin around the event-only route The Magnificent 8. This is a social group ride averaging no more than 3 W/kg with a little race up the reverse Hilly KOM. Stop pedalling after you’ve finished the Zwift KOM to regroup, and we will ride the remainder of the route together.

LEADER'S PACE:
- 2.0 W/kg out of the starting pen (we recommend you warm up to that pace 5 min before the start)
- 2.5-2.7 W/kg on flat sections
- 2.7-3.0 W/kg on climbs

REGROUP:
We regroup after the descent following the Hilly KOM, between km 11-11.3 (before the left turn that takes us to the Fuego Flats). Come to a complete stop until the ride leader announces that we are ready to continue.

WANNA RIDE HARDER?
If you're feeling strong and want to ride harder, a fantastic way to do this with the group is by dropping back to lend a wheel to someone who has fallen off the back for any reason.

You are welcome to join our Discord for the ride: https://discord.gg/3tTtcUm

Please tag @oslodawnpatrol in your Instagram updates.

Information and photos from the ride: https://www.facebook.com/OsloCyclingProject/

So hop on that bike, grab those bottles, and let’s ride!

name: Mountain Massif structured training: Power Development (4 x 4-minutes)
description:
Created by Matt Rowe, from Rowe & King Coaching, this structured training session is designed to help you cycle at a higher intensity, and absorb surges in effort. 


For coaching and all your training needs visit https://roweandking.com/


About the session:
The benefit of this workout is the cumulative fatigue over the whole session, not the max effort of any single interval and is designed to enhance your power.


1. A progressive warmup. 
2. 4-minute TT effort (aim to ride this on feel - get 95% effort out, so you are not totally exhausted after each block) in a heavy gear (this is not a 55-60rpm effort, rather the gear should feel slightly large (e.g. one sprocket top big) i.e. 70-75rpm.  You should pace the effort, aiming to build the intensity throughout the effort to finish strong. Cadence circa 70rpm.
3. 5-minutes easy pedalling.  Repeat steps 2 and 3 a further 3 times (4 efforts in total).


Session details:
Ramp up in 6 steps:
• 3-minutes @ Zone 1-2
• 3-minutes @ Zone 2
• 3-minutes @ Zone 2-3
• 3-minutes @ Zone 2-3
• 3-minutes @ Zone 3
• 3-minutes @ Zone 3-4


Recovery:
• 2-minutes @ Zone 1


Repeat 4 times:
• TT 4-minutes @ Zone 5 (70-75 rpm)
• Easy 5-minutes @ Zone 1


Cool down:
• 4-minutes @ Zone 1


Safety Note:
Only undertake vigorous exercise if you are fit and healthy to do so. If you are at all unsure, consult a Physician or Doctor first.  All training equipment including Bikes and Turbo trainers should be in full working order. Do not use any piece of equipment that does not come up to the required standard.


More information:
For more information check out the Mountain Massif website www.mountainmassif.com, follow on Facebook, Instagram (Mountain_Massif) and join our Zwift Club by clicking the following link https://www.zwift.com/clubs/b639575d-930f-4de6-a79d-bea3313350bc/join.  To record all your training data and chart your progress, consider using the TrainingPeaks app (www.trainingpeaks.com/).

name: INC Relentless Intervals
description:
These regular training sessions will focus on various different areas for improvement in preparation for racing and events over the spring and summer in the Northern Hemisphere.

All sessions will be 60 minutes long and will include a warm up, so just grab your bottles and head straight to the pen. Sessions will vary between Push sessions, designed to lift your FTP with sub-threshold work, for longer periods of time; to Pull sessions, with shorter, harder, intervals above FTP, to “Pull” your FTP up from above.

These are no sweep training rides; if you drop from the group, simply continue the workout on your own or with others of a similar pace. This is an Innovation Cycling Training Ride Event – all riders are welcome. These events are put together to push you further than before, if you are feeling fresh hop on the front, if you need rest surf the draft.

name: ZZRC Bring a Bidon Social Ride
description:
Welcome to our ZZRC Bring a Bidon 2.4-2.7. This is a group ride, not a race, where we encourage riding together.

Our rides are open to all riders, the category enforcement merely allows us to ensure a safe and quality ride for you the riders and for our group.

In 2015 ZZRC was founded and are one of the oldest established clubs on Zwift .

YELLOW BEACON will pace between 2.4-2.7 on the ride , with a possible increase of watts on inclines or sprints , but the average for the whole ride will be as advertised

We strongly promote group riding so on most of our rides we will use the Fence to help encourage that. Using a fence ensures that the ride is not over paced .

In the event of falling off the back of the main group , you will need to pace well over group pace to bridge the gap and catch .

This is where our awesome ZZRC sweeps and Ride Buddies will help you return to group using their draft. They will give you clear encouraging instructions to aid this process .

Our crew are a caring bunch who dedicate a lot of hours to this club , but want you to have the best ride experience on Zwift

You will be fully supported and encouraged throughout the ride by the Leader, Sweeps and Ride Buddies .

Our rides do not allow the use of TT Bikes as they do not draft and will require you to push harder on the ride, and in these instances our Sweeps will not be able to help you .

Mountain bikes operate very similarly, minimum draft so more watts (effort) will be required for the ride and any chase backs to group .

All our rides have a 30 minute late join feature which allows you to rejoin if you have technical issues or you find yourself out of the group in the early stages of the ride. Using this feature SHOULD teleport you back into the main group with our YELLOW BEACON .


We love to have a chat on our rides so join us
on Discord: https://discord.gg/QdeS3PtXTX


TOP TIPS

1) Stay close to the ride leader (or just in front on climbs), don’t let a gap form and the elastic snap!

2) Stay away from the Fence – We don’t like to fry anyone

3) Most important of all . . . HAVE FUN AND ENJOY THE RIDE.

#zzrc

Don’t forget to join our ZZRC-We Pace Not Race Facebook page and our club on the companion app

name: Pride On with LGBTQ Zwifters
description:
LGBTQ Zwifters invite you to ride or race with us during Pride month in support of the LGBTQIA+ community.

Let’s clip in, turn up the colours, and roll out together! This Pride On social ride is all about togetherness - one big, joyful bunch cruising the roads where everyone belongs. No surges, no stress, no getting left behind. You can expect steady spins, good vibes, and plenty of chat as rainbow jerseys fill the screen. Whether you’re here to celebrate, support, or simply enjoy a relaxed ride with an amazing community, this is your space. Ride proud, ride together, and let’s make the miles brighter.


All Pride month events

Group rides:
Most rides will be community-led and rubberbanded (E cat) unless specified by the event pace category.

Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday.
01 - 7 June - Island Hopper
08 - 14 June - Hot Laps
15 - 21 June - Croissant
22 - 28 June - London Flat
29 & 30 June - Beach Island Loop

Sunday.
LGBTQz Ride with Pride club social ride. 

Races:

name: Friday Rocacorba Collective - non-coached workout
description:
Every Thursday, our Training Members are put through their paces by Coach Helen Bridgman, a session that blends structure, intensity, and motivation to get the very best out of your legs.

But why keep all the good stuff to ourselves? Every Friday, we release that same workout for everyone to ride, just jump in when it suits you. Whether you’re chasing watts, building endurance, or just curious to see how we train, this is your chance to experience a Rocacorba Collective session from the inside.

Put on your favourite playlist, settle into the rhythm, and push yourself at your own pace.

Session : Over/Under 3x9

Usual warm up of 5 mins steady, 5 min ramp to threshold and 3 mons recovery before starting the main session.

Workout:
3 x 9 min blocks alternating between
* 1 min Threshold+ @ 103-108% FTP
* 2 min Tempo/SweetSpot @ 80-90% FTP

5 min easy recovery in between blocks (spin light)

Continue for a least 10 mins extra to cool down (spin light the rest of the way home).

This workout sees you accumulating lactate during the over-threshold portions of each block, and then training the body to clear lactate by dropping just below threshold for short periods. This should help with the surges from tempo/SS level in a race, and teach you to recover at that same high level.

eventSubgroups.name: Friday Rocacorba Collective - non-coached workout (C)
eventSubgroups.description:
Every Thursday, our Training Members are put through their paces by Coach Helen Bridgman, a session that blends structure, intensity, and motivation to get the very best out of your legs.

But why keep all the good stuff to ourselves? Every Friday, we release that same workout for everyone to ride, just jump in when it suits you. Whether you’re chasing watts, building endurance, or just curious to see how we train, this is your chance to experience a Rocacorba Collective session from the inside.

Put on your favourite playlist, settle into the rhythm, and push yourself at your own pace.

Session: VO2 6x2 min with sprint finish

Gradual warm up over 6 mins starting at 50% FTP, gradually increasing HR and power to 70% FTP. 5 x 30s on and 30s off to really get the HR going!

The main blocks are 6 x 2 min VO2 Max with a 20s sprint at the end and 5 min recoveries in between. Try to do these on a hill if you can. Stay seated for the 2 min VO2 and get out of the saddle for the 20s sprint at the end.

Cool down for 10 min easy at the end.

This session will help increase your peak aerobic power, make you more aerobically efficient and improve your endurance.

name: FRR Weekend Warrior Series - ITT
description:
Flamme Rouge Racing are excited to bring you our WEEKEND WARRIOR which build on the Classica races and the full series to mid August.

Each event will offer 3 races Friday to Sunday, using three formats - iTT / Scratch / Points - each race will convert to points, based on segments and finish - a riders points total will be drawn from all 3 races, do more, score more!

Each event will center around the type of course and terrain of the monument, with the actual race day event being of a length that is fitting for the monument.

Classica races are part of the FRR Weekend Warrior Race Series for which there will be at least 10 WW events, refer to website for the Schedule and rules:

Series Schedule
https://flammerougeracing.com/race-schedule/

Rules
https://flammerougeracing.com/race-rules

Event Basics
- Public events - MIXED RACING
- Five Max 30day ZRS ranged pens
- Mandatory racing experience - HRM - Smart Trainers


- Season long Order of Merit (OoM)
- Best 7 scoring events to count (an event counts the points from all 3 races over

FRR Registered riders form the OoM - Top 10 earn prizes on condition they are FRR Subscribers 

For all details, registration and how to become an FRR subscriber vist our website:
https://flammerougeracing.com/

Primary Communication via DISCORD

Discord - RACE channel for questions, updates and lively chat - it is by far the best place to clarify or report anything during the series

Invite link: https://discord.com/invite/nQNWHQK6PS

Smart Trainers - HRM
- Smart Trainers are mandatory
- Race Control can verify with the Zwift platform 
- HRMs are mandatory

So be SMART and use a SMART trainer as your PRIMARY power source where you can....

FRR Code of Conduct
- We expect the best racing behavior from all riders, if riders have an issue then always contact race control via email first, we will investigate every request raised.
- In race we do not expect riders to abuse others, flag, report to race control, screen shot etc.... riders who ignore this will be DQ'd for the season
- Discord chat remains objective and banter - anything more will be removed and warnings/bans will be issued

And finally remember we all do this for fun and exercise so ride on and enjoy the FRR events....stay safe and if it starts to hurt then welcome to the fun zone...! 
(But stop if it really does hurt too much please!)

name: OTR Snap Crackle Pop Punch Time
description:
Snap Crackle Pop Punch Time is a group ride, race & interval training all rolled into one fun challenging event. Unique “race” scoring, where results in ZwiftPower are based on sum of segment times on a route with punchy climbs and/or sprints. Group rides together at ~2wkg, and ride leader provides guidance and lead-outs to smash a segment; then regroup, rinse & repeat. New route every week.

Multiple time slots on Fri-Sun, including Fri Atlantic, Sun APAC and Sun Americas/EMEA.
Riders need to join ZwiftPower.com to see their results as sum of segment times.

Event links: https://www.zwift.com/events/tag/snapcracklepop
Weekly results (across all time slots): https://zwiftpower.com/league.php?id=2656
In-ride conversation (“SCP Ride” channel): https://discord.gg/B52qdExaW2
Chat, banter and results: https://discord.gg/HNzvx98srF

Group ride with all cats together at ~2w/kg. Yellow beacon / ride leader (when present) will provide instructions for each segment, and drop the fence when it's time to punch/sprint. Fence is for guidance only (non-zapping).

Ride at a relaxed pace between the timed segments.
Work together to optimize draft for faster segment times.
Slow or stop with yellow beacon after each segment to regroup.

All categories start in a single pen.
Results split per WKG category in ZwiftPower.
No power ups, default drafting, no TT bikes.

One of our regular SCP routes is 3.5 laps of Innsbruckring, with 4x Leg Snappers plus 3x sprints (stopping to regroup on the kicker in between). The challenge is to achieve sub 4 mins for the sum of 7 segment times for cats A/B (that's 45 secs per snapper plus 20 secs per sprint), sub 5 mins for cat C, and sub 7 mins for cat D. Best time to beat is 3:33.
Historical results for Leg Snapper: https://zwiftpower.com/league.php?id=1322

name: FRR Weekend Warrior Series - ITT
description:
Flamme Rouge Racing are excited to bring you our WEEKEND WARRIOR which build on the Classica races and the full series to mid August.

Each event will offer 3 races Friday to Sunday, using three formats - iTT / Scratch / Points - each race will convert to points, based on segments and finish - a riders points total will be drawn from all 3 races, do more, score more!

Each event will center around the type of course and terrain of the monument, with the actual race day event being of a length that is fitting for the monument.

Classica races are part of the FRR Weekend Warrior Race Series for which there will be at least 10 WW events, refer to website for the Schedule and rules:

Series Schedule
https://flammerougeracing.com/race-schedule/

Rules
https://flammerougeracing.com/race-rules

Event Basics
- Public events - MIXED RACING
- Five Max 30day ZRS ranged pens
- Mandatory racing experience - HRM - Smart Trainers


- Season long Order of Merit (OoM)
- Best 7 scoring events to count (an event counts the points from all 3 races over

FRR Registered riders form the OoM - Top 10 earn prizes on condition they are FRR Subscribers 

For all details, registration and how to become an FRR subscriber vist our website:
https://flammerougeracing.com/

Primary Communication via DISCORD

Discord - RACE channel for questions, updates and lively chat - it is by far the best place to clarify or report anything during the series

Invite link: https://discord.com/invite/nQNWHQK6PS

Smart Trainers - HRM
- Smart Trainers are mandatory
- Race Control can verify with the Zwift platform 
- HRMs are mandatory

So be SMART and use a SMART trainer as your PRIMARY power source where you can....

FRR Code of Conduct
- We expect the best racing behavior from all riders, if riders have an issue then always contact race control via email first, we will investigate every request raised.
- In race we do not expect riders to abuse others, flag, report to race control, screen shot etc.... riders who ignore this will be DQ'd for the season
- Discord chat remains objective and banter - anything more will be removed and warnings/bans will be issued

And finally remember we all do this for fun and exercise so ride on and enjoy the FRR events....stay safe and if it starts to hurt then welcome to the fun zone...! 
(But stop if it really does hurt too much please!)

name: DIRT Friday Morning Sprintapalooza v2
description:
Welcome to the DIRT Friday Morning Sprintapalooza!

Please join us weekly on Fridays to stretch those sprinting muscles with
some of the fastest on Zwift. The beacon will ride at a consistent 2.5w/kg
and call out sprints, typically hitting 4 to 8 per ride. Power-ups are
limited to aero only and our large bunch results in relaxed recovery and a
big, drafty lead-in. You smash the sprint, sag to the beacon, recover, and
repeat!! We will typically ride the same route for several weeks, giving
you a chance to dial in the optimal start location for each sprint, before
moving on to a new location. We will try to highlight popular race routes
and get practice in for upcoming ZRL race locations. Are you strong enough
to be counted in the top 3 this week?!

Our ride includes a 30 minute late join option, so jump in with us and
don’t be afraid of losing your wheel.

Team DIRT is an acronym for Dads Indoors Riding Trainers. Our group exists
to encourage and build up cyclists around the world no matter your time
zone, fitness level, pro or amateur. We exist to encourage and build up a
team culture of unity in the cycling community, especially among moms and
dads who put personal fitness and health high on their agenda.

name: GRIT - HARD TRUTH
description:
Welcome to the Hard Truth climb. This ride will always cover long climbs on big mountains.
We invite you to take training to the next level by adding this ride to your weekly routine. Steep climbs are hard and long steep climbs are really hard, that is the Hard Truth of this ride.

The ride will start with a friendly group ride format with riders staying together before the big climbs start. Enjoy this social time on the ride before the Hard Truth of the climb arrives.

On climbs, strong riders at the front will push the pace and ride at race pace to compete for the win and the best KOM time. Strong riders at the front will likely output over 5 wpk on the climb.

To keep with a more social ride format, many riders will form a group and ride together on the climb. This social group will likely be using power typical of a Cat B ride. Riders are encouraged to find a group and ride together to help each other survive the Hard Truth of these big climbs.

name: KISS at Base Training Ride
description:
Join us to work on your endurance and power output at your aerobic threshold (AT) in Zone 2. The exercise will give you endurance and increased performance using fat as energy. A well-developed AT can give you better race performance increase the amount of time before your body uses glycogen stores.

We are now offering three separate paced rides to better accommodate various fitness levels.

The B Cat is for riders with Zone 2 between 3.2 - 3.99 w/kg.
The C Cat is for riders with Zone 2 between 2.5 - 3.19 w/kg.
The D Cat is for riders with Zone 2 between 2.2 - 2.49 w/kg.

Remember this when you approach hills and inclines along the way. Stick together to enjoy the draft and companionship. The ride leader will not exceed the advertised pace at any time - even on hills. Please keep an eye on the leader beacon (yellow) and the sweeper beacon (red) to stay in the blob.

So turn on your graph (press G on computer keyboard or select it from on-screen menu in iOS and Android) and paint it blue. Give the body a good foundation for Zwift racing. Discord server Link: https://discord.gg/kBmXhY2

name: CRYO-GEN Peaky Friday.
description:
The CRYO-GEN Peaky Friday Ride is a social ride for everyone who enjoys a
good climb, with plenty of rolling routes mixed in for variety. Join us
each Friday for a friendly, social spin that offers something for every
type of rider.

Whether you’re a steady D cat rider looking for supportive group miles and
a bit of extra hill practice, or a stronger rider after a fun, relaxed spin
with the option to stretch your legs on the climbs, you’ll find your place
on The Peaky Friday Ride. It’s all about teamwork, good vibes, and enjoying
the ride together, wherever the road takes us!

The yellow beacon will pace at around 2.2 w/kg on the flats and 2.5 w/kg on
the climbs. At times, we’ll turn off the fence and open up a free-pace
section, giving everyone the chance to push harder if they wish, or simply
ride steady with the yellow beacon, who will always maintain the advertised
pace. We regroup at the KOM banner, with plenty of notice before the fence
is reactivated, so everyone can come back together and enjoy the ride as a
group.

For those who enjoy a touch of luxury, we even have a Limo Service run by a
member of the sweep team! This friendly gruppetto offers a more relaxed
pace when needed, ensuring everyone can enjoy the ride at their own rhythm.

All we ask is that you respect the ride leader, help where you can, and
keep it fun and social. We hope you will join us on the hills!

HEALTH: We would advise any rider who is attempting a Zwift ride for the
first time to ensure that their health should always take precedence over
completing any ride. If you feel unwell or unable to continue please STOP

NOTE: Exercise contributes to 25% weight loss; Healthy Eating (Not Diet)
contributes to the other 75%. Be fit and Healthy.

name: The XP Express
description:
All aboard The XP Express!

We're dishing out Double XP in this event so sign up, kit up and get ready to Level Up.

The XP Express is a turbocharged ride where every pedal stroke counts twice. Whether you're starting your Zwift journey or a seasoned pro, hop aboard to Level Up your ride.

How does it work?
The XP Express events will double your XP, helping you wrack up 40XP per kilometer or 64XP per mile! Leveling Up is the perfect way to unlock new swag, access to bikes and wheels, new routes and, of course, some bragging rights.

Use this event as an easy recovery ride, a quick warm up before your next race or push yourself to the limit to see how much XP you can earn.

description: All aboard The XP Express! We're dishing out Double XP in this event so sign up, lace up your shoes and get ready to Level Up. name: DWGZ Friday Surprise!
description:
Welcome!  DWGZ Surprise ride is like a box of chocolates. You never know what you’re gonna get!  Will we sprint? Will we climb? Badge hunting? Who knows! Each week there will be a new adventure.

Join the DWGZ (Determined Whitty Gritty Zwifters) every Friday as we adventure together and best of all you can help choose what we ride the following week.

The yellow beacon will roll at approximately 2.8125 w/kg with some of the best red sweeper beacons in Zwift!
While this ride is about variety, the DWGZ are about culture. We’re a global crew of cyclists who thrive on shared suffering, do hard stuff, lift each other up, and radiate good energy. We ride six days a week at 6:05 AM Eastern US time, building a strong, global cycling community grounded in grit, humor, and heart.

Late join available for 30 minutes — jump in anytime!

name: Stage 2: Level Up Racing: BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits
description:
Level Up Racing is June’s ZRacing monthly series. Race across five stages from June 1 to July 5, with a new route each week and up to 250 XP waiting at every banner. Complete stages to build series progress, chase the GC leaderboard, and grab bonus XP as you race.

Stage 2

Dates: June 8–14
Route: BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits
Laps: 1
Distance: 22.1 km
Elevation: 243 m

Stage 2 brings BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits, a punchier test with more elevation and more chances to keep building XP. One lap, one effort, and another shot to add to your series total.

MONTHLY GC COMPETITION

Looking for extra motivation? The Monthly GC (General Classification) Competition lets you track your progress across all stages. Each race counts—your times add up throughout the series, shaping the overall standings. At the end of the month, the fastest total time takes the win!

name: TGIF DIRTy Goats
description:
If screaming legs and burning lungs make you smile. Welcome to DIRTy Goats.

Every Friday, we encourage you to leave the flats behind and embrace the challenge of the weekly KOM.

An inclusive ride for all wanting to improve their mental toughness, develop climbing technique or simply badge hunt the routes you frequently choose to avoid. DIRTy Goats is the team to motivate you out of your comfort zone.

If you are daunted by the DIRTy Goats, Yellow beacon will stay within the ride limits. Our pace is based on a 75kg rider, riding 2.6w/kg or 195 watts on the flat, and 3.5w/kg or 260 watts on the climb. Lighter and heavier riders wanting to pace with the Leader are asked to adjust their power to work together.

Each ride will target 1000 vertical meters. This is not always achievable within our 90 minute ride, but the team will often keep rolling until we hit our goal.

Stronger riders are encouraged to work with the beacons to help the group. But if you really must fly, we ask that you move away quickly during the warm-up to avoid pulling the front.

Team DIRT is an acronym for Dads Inside Riding Trainers. This group has grown and brought like-minded moms and dads together who love to make time for Zwift around work and family.

Please join us on discord: https://discord.gg/sUnwqPZ

And Facebook at: https://www.facebook.com/groups/ZWIFTDIRT

name: Stage 2: Level Up Racing: BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits
description:
Level Up Racing is June’s ZRacing monthly series. Race across five stages from June 1 to July 5, with a new route each week and up to 250 XP waiting at every banner. Complete stages to build series progress, chase the GC leaderboard, and grab bonus XP as you race.

Stage 2

Dates: June 8–14
Route: BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits
Laps: 1
Distance: 22.1 km
Elevation: 243 m

Stage 2 brings BRAEk-fast Crits and Grits, a punchier test with more elevation and more chances to keep building XP. One lap, one effort, and another shot to add to your series total.

MONTHLY GC COMPETITION

Looking for extra motivation? The Monthly GC (General Classification) Competition lets you track your progress across all stages. Each race counts—your times add up throughout the series, shaping the overall standings. At the end of the month, the fastest total time takes the win!

VIEW RESULTS: http://zwift.com/racing/leagues/zracingjun2026
—------------------
Zwift Racing Score is aimed at pairing you with riders of similar racing abilities to keep racing fun, fair, and competitive. Read the FAQ here: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/racing-score-faq-BkG9_Rqrh


ADVANCED CATEGORY = 650+
CATEGORY RANGE 1 = 0-159 | 160-269 | 270-389 | 390-509 | 510-649
CATEGORY RANGE 2 = 0-209 | 210-329 | 330-449 | 450-569 | 570-724

For riders with a Racing Score of 650 or higher, the' Advanced' category will have separate events scheduled every other hour.

Please note that in order to enter the Advanced category, you will need the following:
Heart Rate Monitor
Zwift Racing Score of over 650
Smart Trainer/Bike or Power Meter


Hourly ZRacing will be split into five tighter categories for more exciting competition. Plus, with hourly alternating category ranges, you’ll have more options to find races that suit your level.

name: Bike MS - Eventful 40 Friday
description:
In addition to our monthly dual jersey unlock rides Bike MS is all about exploring together, so let's explore those event only routes. This 40 minute group ride will rotate different routes for those badge hunters out there. Lead beacon will ride around 2.0, but come for the journey and unlock a kit along the way. 
Bike MS Season if right around the corner, so let's connect over a ride as we prepare for the adventures ahead. Multiple Sclerosis does not stop, so neither will we as we ride together for this great cause.
Bike MS is the largest charity cycling series across the United States consisting of 50 rides and raising over $50 million in 2023 for the National MS Society. Bike MS supports the National MS Society's mission to Cure MS while empowering all people affected by MS to live their best lives. Whether you want to cross the Finish Line in person or take on a new challenge from anywhere — there’s a Bike MS event that’s right for you! 
Check out www.bikeMS.org and experience the ride of your life. Use Zwift24 for a discount on your Bike MS Ride entry fee.
Come join us for weekly Club Rides: Bike MS ZC
#dontjustride #bikeMS #whateverittakes #strongertogether
